reviews.author: Matt Y.
reviews.text: One of the best campgrounds. I really liked the new 1 week out booking as it made it easier for us to book several sites for our group. This site was quiet and next to a small creek. Nobody ever came to the site next to this one (H15) so we had a lot more privacy. This site is really close to site H15. But otherwise one of the best being at the very end of the road!

reviews.author: Odessa M.
reviews.text:
First, I want to start with, the campground is beautiful, large sites, bear boxes, picnic bench, and a fire ring on every site. 
The poor star rating is for our particular site C006 has an unmarked trail to a beach off the river (the true entrance to this is near D loop) and we dealt with people, probably close to a hundred on our 2 night/3 day stay trampling through our site to get to said beach. It did not matter if we were on site, multiple groups would be coming through. It really put me off this campground, and I will not be returning. We had one person mess up our $700 Big Agnes Copper Spur tent lines up with said trampling. It really was a nightmare, and put me completely off ever returning to this camp ground. Such inconsiderate humans here.

reviews.author: bruce c.
reviews.text: Great place

reviews.author: Amanda L.
reviews.text: Great campground with well stocked restrooms and fire circles/stoves.

reviews.author: Wendy V.
reviews.text: I visited in mid-September, so good campsites were available, first come-first served. The campground was relatively clean and restrooms were acceptable. The staff were friendly and helpful. I drove up to Paradise in the morning, but it was so crowded that the nearest parking was 2 miles away, so I went on several shorter hikes elsewhere. I highly recommend the Silver Falls loop, which begins and ends at Ohanapacosh. It rolls through a beautiful forest, with plenty of creeks, waterfalls, moss and massive boulders. The only negative was the constant annoying tourist helicopter flights overhead throughout the afternoon, I think rich people can do without helicopter rides at Mt. Rainier.

reviews.author: Pamela P.
reviews.text:
The reservation system had just switched to FF, First Come/First Served, when I decided to camp. I wasn't sure how that would work but I trusted in the system. As I drove up to the Visitor Center a large white board signed explained everything. I checked in with Park Staff and was quickly able to reserve my favorite site from my previous on line review. Staff assured me that I had a good site. I was very pleased when the Staff member asked if I had my senior access pass for the Park. I did and received 1/2 off the site cost. Nice surprise.
I found the grounds clean, quiet, and well maintained. The Staff must work very hard because there were not a lot of them on duty. 
I would love to see Grove of the Patriarch again. It's been since the 1980's I believe. I read it was closed indefinitely.

reviews.author: Kelly H.
reviews.text: Super clean and great views.  Had the whole place to myself.

reviews.author: Angela F.
reviews.text: Great home base for exploring Mt Rainier Sunrise area.  Clean comfortable camp, so quiet, so dark at night!

reviews.author: Chad B.
reviews.text: Could not reserve campsite until 3pm. Had to sit in campsite until ranger could assign reservations. We came to see the park, not sit in the campground all afternoon.

reviews.author: Caity H.
reviews.text: Nice and quiet campground with helpful park rangers :)

reviews.author: Lauren Y.
reviews.text: The H loop is for introverts lol.  Best loop IMO!  There is a lovely trail to the creek from the  H22 campsite, and I spent an entire afternoon reading on my camp chair with my feet in the water. Absolutely magical!

reviews.author: Cody H.
reviews.text: So beautiful and I will return the only thing that is not good is people driving through the campground really fast and almost hitting my kid more than once with multiple people and also other kids and not caring that they are playing

reviews.author: Adriana G.
reviews.text: Beautiful camp site with good parking space and plenty of room for tents as well as room for tables and cooking. Close to the restroom area and overlooking a small creek. Only a small walk down to the river, day area, and hiking spots. Great weekend spent here!

reviews.author: Tasha U.
reviews.text: The campground itself is beautiful, the river is breathtaking, and the staff we encountered were kind and knowledgeable.

reviews.author: Kathleen H.
reviews.text: Beautiful, quiet campsite, with very respectful neighbors. We ended up moving to a first come-first serve site since we didn't realize that H loop didn't have bear lockers for food and cooking equipment, we scored an amazing site right on the river. The bathrooms were all clean and well stocked. My daughter loved walking through the visitor center and the maps to nearby hikes with difficulty ratings was really appreciated. The rangers at the campsite registry office were also super helpful and very friendly. There's Wi-Fi at the visitor center, even after it's closed, so it's really easy to log in and purchase a vehicle reservation for the next day for Paradise or Sunrise when they're available at 7pm. The trail to Silver Falls is accessed from the campground and was an easy, but totally worth it hike with some cute little wooden bridges over laughing creek. Definitely keeping this one in the rotation!

reviews.author: Romeo D.
reviews.text: Great camping site. My kids enjoy our stay and the nearby trail going to the Silver falls. Neighborhood site is respectful and quite feels like we owned the whole national park. Kudos!

reviews.author: jeremy d.
reviews.text: Really nice campground. New WiFi access at the visitor center is a huge upgrade and really appreciated. I think the first come first serve sites in A loop are the best.

reviews.author: Joelene S.
reviews.text: First time staying in Mt. Ranier National Park and decided to try this first come first serve first, not knowing what to expect. Well, this campground exceeded our expectations. Not only were the grounds beautiful with old growth trees, but add in the river and the hiking and the NPS Rangers and employees and you got yourself a fantastic experience! Our site was in Loop A, (the FC, FS sites) close to the restrooms and a hop skip jump to the visitor center where you could use their free WiFi if needed since there’s no cell reception. The rangers were incredibly helpful, access to the park was so close (but you still need timed entry passes) and although no hookups were provided, it was a fantastic stay for us! We are already excited to come back and try some other hikes!

reviews.author: john  l.
reviews.text: Clean facilities and grounds. Sites are thoughtfully placed. Staff is very professional. Other campers were unusually quiet and respectful. Would definitely visit again.

reviews.author: Jim P.
reviews.text: Very nice campground. Nice hike to Solver Falls.

reviews.author: Stephanie W.
reviews.text: We selected Saturday on reservation. My fault for not triple checking. We somehow got Friday. 6 hours after arriving we were unceremoniously kicked out. My kids crying and screaming. Wonderful first experience

reviews.author: Seth R.
reviews.text: Cannot rate this highly enough. This ks the best spot in the park and the park itself is wonderful.

reviews.author: David L.
reviews.text: Walks around visitor center is like walking in fairy land.  There are also hot springs along the trail

reviews.author: Piper C.
reviews.text: Special place

reviews.author: Clare G.
reviews.text: What an incredible location. The site (loop H site 007) was perfect, but a little higher off the road loop and not super close to other sites. The forest sound feels so muted but other voices and sound can travel a lot because it’s so quiet from the leaves and plants. Some groups nearby were laughing and talking loudly enough to be bothered but we went to sleep pretty early so they quieted down eventually. The bathrooms are pretty basic but definitely seemed like there were several for easy access from any part of the campgrounds. I did not have cell service (Comcast Xfinity) at the campsite (fine by me! but good to know). It’s about a 45 min drive to the Paradise lot… we left camp around 5:15am to beat the crowds and because we hadn’t been able to get a timed entry reservation ahead of time, and were able to enter the park and get a parking spot without a problem. Highly recommend doing that if you’re able to and if you’re planning to visit during the peak season. Would love to come back! :)

reviews.author: Linda  J.
reviews.text: Some of the bridges were in poor condition on the trails

reviews.author: Remy C.
reviews.text:
Great spot, located in a beautiful forest with great hiking and even a chrystal clear river flowing through the camp.
Also very close to Paradise & Sunrise Mount Rainier entrances.
There is no signal so be prepared to be out of camp at 7pm if you have to book for a timed entry reservation for the park! (There is a brewery in Packwood which was perfect for us to answer that need!)
Toilets were well maintained

reviews.author: Joe K.
reviews.text: The campground was beautiful but we had trouble getting to the restrooms because there was a group with several tents blocking the stairs up to them. We are in our 60's & 70's and walking up the hill over logs, etc in the dark was difficult (especially in the pouring rain. Wifi at the visitor center was nice to have.

reviews.author: Todd A.
reviews.text: Beautifu, large spot close to the water and lots of room for different tent configurations.

reviews.author: Morgan  S.
reviews.text: Our group went tent camping at the Ohanapecosh campground the bathrooms were great! Always were clean and they had paper towels.

reviews.author: Tommy D.
reviews.text: I stayed in the C loop site 33. It was a great campsite and mellow due to the fire ban. There's a swimming spot in the river by the picnic area. The water was cold but really nice on a hot day.

reviews.author: Mark Z.
reviews.text: We stayed at H13, it was a very nice campground although a little close to H14. The tent lot was pretty big and even.

reviews.author: John T.
reviews.text: Great place with kids, lost if room to play and ride bikes and lots of trails to hike.  I only wish our site had bear boxes for food like many of the other sites did.

reviews.author: Eamon B.
reviews.text: Fantastic, beautiful campsite, lush, great access to walks, visitor centre close by 10/10 recommend.

reviews.author: Prathyusha P.
reviews.text: Stunning and clean place..so close and true to nature. The place is clean , close to car parking and close to a 1 hour walk to waterfall. We camped here and totally loved the place. Heaven on earth

reviews.author: Carrie M.
reviews.text:
Overall, we really enjoyed our stay at Ohanapecosh; it is a beautiful campground with great access to nearby trails and the Paradise corridor. The river is so beautiful and easy to access as well for some water play. Our campsite was really nice and not too far from restroom or the river. 

The only negatives I saw were that I don't believe the bathroom was cleaned daily, I believe a lot of people book sites and then cancel them (it was hard to get multiple sites for groups - timeframe I wanted only had 4 sites available to book that were scattered, but ultimately, sites were empty next to us during our stay), and I wish there was a shower. Regarding bathroom, in three nights we stayed, I think it was only cleaned once. There were lots of bugs in the sink every morning. I also wish that Mt Rainier would allow dogs on their trails to responsible pet owners. :)  

Overall, we would still definitely come back.

reviews.author: Victoria W.
reviews.text: Breezy, the ranger who helped us was amazing! Our campgrounds were so clean and nice, and it was the perfect place for our family trip

reviews.author: Sheila G.
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful campgrounds we've ever seen, and close to so many great sites in Ranier.

reviews.author: Diane S.
reviews.text:
Beautiful tall trees and turquoise river. Cell phone coverage at the visitors center, if you need it. I’d recommend both  H7 and F8. We stayed one night at each. Both were really nice, on the edge of wilderness, secluded sites. 

While you’re there, check out the visitors center, the hot springs loop and Silver Falls (about 2.5 miles round trip, pretty flat). We went up to Paradise after 3, no reservation needed, no line.

reviews.author: Ivan D.
reviews.text: The campground was great, but the campsite wasn't, nor was the timed entry aspect. The campsite (D014) said it had a 13' x 14' tentpad, so we thought was going to be great for our 10'x14' rectangular tent. Turns out, it was an octagonal tent pad that not at all 13'x14'. We were unable to use the tentpad, so we were forced to stake our tent down in the fireplace area of the campsite, which had significantly harder ground than the nice sandy octagonal tentpad. D014 is also a fishbowl of a campsite, and we always felt like we were right on top of the adjacent campsites. It was very conveniently close to the water (about 15 feet), and the bathrooms, but there was no path from the far side of the loop to get to the water and bathrooms so most people from those other sites ended up essentially walking through our campsite to get there. The other truly significant complaint is that there's no service, which ordinarily I wouldn't complain about for a campsite, except that if you want to go into any of the other areas of Mount Rainier, you HAVE to get a timed entry pass the night before. When we checked in, the rangers helpfully said that there was WiFi at the visitor center, and there was, but not a single person there was able to get onto the Recreation.gov website to get a timed entry. I was forced to call a relative halfway across the country to get them to use their home computer to book a timed entry when I needed it. By the end of the stay, the rangers were recommending that people drive to Packwood to use their cell service, which is pretty ridiculous. If I'm paying to stay at a National Park Campsite, it should come with a way to get me into the National Park that I'm staying at. The rangers themselves were very helpful and nice, and the visitor center was small but appreciated by my kids. There's a way to get down to the river and we saw multiple people swimming there at various times. There were some short hikes right on the campground that my family enjoyed.

reviews.author: Hugh Clark M.
reviews.text: Great park !

reviews.author: Rose C.
reviews.text: We camped at H006 with an 18' trailer. There was barely room for the trailer and our truck. It would not hold a 27' trailer. The campsite was beautiful. The many Douglas Fir trees were stately and gorgeous. The hike to Silver Falls was beautiful and easy.

reviews.author: Tessa R.
reviews.text: This is one of our favorite campgrounds - amazing rangers, hosts, lots of space to roam and explore, access to trails...it's all amazing. We try to come back every year. Thanks for everything!

reviews.author: Amy J.
reviews.text: The Rangers were very helpful in finding another spot when our trailer was unable to back into our original spot. The Campground was beautiful but spaces were close together and people were loud at night and woke our baby several times. I wouldn't call this place dog friendly. They were very strict about them being on a 6ft or less leash and dogs couldn't enjoy any of the trails or water with us. They couldn't even chase a ball to burn some energy.

reviews.author: Sari S.
reviews.text: Absolutely amazing campground all around! Must see and experience!

reviews.author: Irina K.
reviews.text: We enjoyed our stay at Ohanapecosh! Loved the local trails, swimming in the river, visitor's center.

reviews.author: shuqin z.
reviews.text: The clean restroom , the big campsite in the fantastic forest and the little creek nearby make our stay happy

reviews.author: Raymond v.
reviews.text: The campground is in a very convenient location to visit Mt Rainier NP. Don't forget to also get timed entry tickets. The spots were not very clearly marked and a bit chaotically laid out, so we were not exactly sure where to put up our tent. The toilets were not very clean and some of them were clogged. It is nice to swim at the river and you'll see a lot of families with kids here.

reviews.author: Michael K.
reviews.text: I enjoyed the campground but was extremely put off by limitations entering the park.

reviews.author: Sara P.
reviews.text:
This is one of our favorite campgrounds! It's private and right next to the river. The sound of the water was the perfect lull to sleep. We spent two nights here and it was the perfect stop to see both Paradise & Sunrise side of the park. The wifi at the Visitor's Center allowed us to have a little service amidst gaps across most of the park. We would absolutely stay here again!
Pros: 
Location was one of the more private sites in our loop
Bear box on site
Room for two mid-size tents and relatively flat space
Playing in the river was a HUGE win for our kids

Cons:
Bathrooms weren't the best in the CLoop, but the Visitor's Center was a little cleaner.

reviews.author: Michele L.
reviews.text: A wonderful campground.  The river is cold but great swimming for sure.  The Silver Falls loop makes a great after dinner hiker.

reviews.author: Richard D.
reviews.text: Beautiful location, the river that runs through has a swimming hole and a little sandy beach!  There are no showers in the bathroom--which are grossly in need of new fixtures and sinks, but they are 'cleaned' every day.  This is a bear campground so be prepared to keep all food-smelling items in the bear box at each campsite at all times.  There is internet at the campground office right by the front door where many people congregated, but not in the rest of the site.  Overall, an exceptional campground.  Our site was C22 and backed up to one of two group sites, so there was a lot of late noise.

reviews.author: Tara D.
reviews.text: This was a big site that offered great privacy and a relaxing atmosphere with the creek and nearby rush of the river. Bring a swimsuit and water shoes to take advantage of swimming in the river!

reviews.author: Morgan  B.
reviews.text: A little buggy in the evening, but that is expected since there is a river and old growth forest. The rangers at the visitor center are helpful, and the bathrooms are clean. Ohanapecosh is really cute and quaint campground, and I would absolutely stay here again.

reviews.author: Mercedes K.
reviews.text:
I really like this campground. The staff is so amazing and helpful. I like the location. It is so convenient to go to Paradise and easy drive to other locations. I felt safe. 
Here’s a hint: if there is not a site for all your days, book for one day, then get up early and snag an A site (they are first come, first serve). I was able to stay 5 full days during a busy time!

reviews.author: Cynthia C.
reviews.text: I have been camping at Ohanapecosh for more than 30 years. It's a family destination. So sad that the ranger talks in the amphitheater do not exist. Why not? We have enjoyed the star gazing talks during the new moon in August but it has not been presented in years. And, sooooooo many campsites are closed due to "dangerous trees". Every downed tree I saw was healthy. What a loss.

reviews.author: Foster T.
reviews.text: The river is great. The campground was very smoky from camp fires my daughter has asthma we had to leave.  It would be super if folks just had campfires when it is not summer

reviews.author: Sebastian  A.
reviews.text: We loved staying here. Big ole Douglas Firs, rivers and babbling creeks. Whats not to love?

reviews.author: Kayla  O.
reviews.text: I have been visiting Ohanapecosh for years and it has been our favorite campground in all of Washington. My recent visit was slightly disappointing. Not once did we see a park ranger driving through the campground, and the bathrooms were dirty and often out of paper towels. They now have WiFi at the Visitor Center so you can do timed entry, but it crashes once too many join. It is a beautiful campground but is not being maintained as well as it used to be.

reviews.author: Alina G.
reviews.text: little privacy, sites a bit small

reviews.author: Donna C.
reviews.text: This site was beautiful and close to the restrooms. It was a fairly open site and not a very private, however we loved loved the beautiful towering trees so much it didn't bother us.

reviews.author: Virginia B.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground, very quiet at night despite having a large number of campers present. Our campsite C22 had a wonderful trail to the river which could be heard from our tent. We would love to stay at this site again.

reviews.author: Sheri W.
reviews.text: We love Ohanapacosh!

reviews.author: Brian P.
reviews.text: Great classic campground!!  Really appreciated the non-trampled vegetation separating the sites.

reviews.author: Cynthia G.
reviews.text: The campground itself is nice. I was a little disappointed that there weren't more trails out of the campground. It seems that most of the other activities in Mt. Rainier National Park are a good hour drive away. This is the only campground we stayed at in the park, so I can't compare it to others. However, next time I would choose a different campground.

reviews.author: Fred H.
reviews.text: Great camping and very clean! Thankful for a very quiet park at night!

reviews.author: Cayley T.
reviews.text: Convenient location for access to both corridors. Spacious and private campsites, very shady. Bathrooms were buggy compared to other campsites in the national parks

reviews.author: Jenny M.
reviews.text: This campground is beautiful and it's nice to have the visitor center, access to hikes and the river right there. The bathrooms are outdated and overused probably, but it really didn't matter since we loved the rest of the campground so much. We loved walking down to the river and playing in the water or just sitting and listening to the sound of it.

reviews.author: Shirley C.
reviews.text: We've been camping at Ohanapecosh for over 40 years and never get tired of it. We pitched two 9x9 tents at site D10. The tent pads sloped a bit, but we compensated by sleeping with our heads uphill. The parking pad is just barely big enough for two cars. This site is on a hill overlooking fallen logs and a creek that flows into the Ohanapecosh River. Our grandchildren (11 and 13) had a wonderful time climbing on the logs and exploring the creek bed. The short hike to scenic Silver Falls is perfect for families with children. We appreciate the revisions that have been made in the reservations system, making it easier for families to plan a camping trip within a shorter window of time.

reviews.author: Kari S.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground!!!

reviews.author: Christie C.
reviews.text: We come back to Ohanapecosh campground because we love the beauty, the peace, and the facilities. The people are wonderful.

reviews.author: Vignesh D.
reviews.text: Very lush full forest and beautiful campground. We had a campsite beside river(A13, D6). You can book the campsite prior or also go for First come first serve.You have few hikes too. One of the beat campground experiences we had.

reviews.author: Brendan B.
reviews.text: My wife, daughter and I had a great time visiting Rainer National Park and staying at Ohanapecosh! We loved our spot in the campground and will definitely be back.

reviews.author: Richard P.
reviews.text: Great campground, hard to reserve a spot.

reviews.author: Linda V.
reviews.text: Peaceful and beautiful. Staff was helpful and nice. Waterfall hike right out of camp was gorgeous!

reviews.author: Tod H.
reviews.text: If you’re not back country camping this is where you want to be!!

reviews.author: Theresa T.
reviews.text: I love Ohanapocesh camping.  It’s very family friendly and peaceful.

reviews.author: elisabella t.
reviews.text: Our second year camping here and we love all that it offers

reviews.author: McCalester L.
reviews.text: Site C10 is large but the table and fire pit are incredibly close to the neighboring site. The trail to the amazing swim hole in the river is right next to this site so expect hundreds of people walking by on a busy Saturday. Maneuvering my small trailer was slightly impaired by how close the garbage station is to the driveway. Silver falls is worth the walk- we passed about about 50 other folks on the trail. There are flush toilets here.  My daughter liked the ranger station there are a lot of stuffed creatures. I tried to get a next day permit for Sunset and Paradise by using the WiFi at the station at the 7 pm release but it wouldn’t work. Overall a good experience but we probably won’t come back.

reviews.author: Mark S.
reviews.text: We loved this campground!  The layout, access to trails, park store, and proximity to the river all made this a great experience.  While the restrooms could be updated, they were always clean.  After camping in close to a dozen national parks, Ohanapecosh is one of our favorites.

reviews.author: M r.
reviews.text:
We spent 2 days tent camping during one of western Washington's summer "heat domes". While being very rustic it is a beautiful place , and restful. Night was clear and star filled.  The Ohanapecosh river flows through the campground and provided a cool tranquil place to sit during the heat of the day. The water is too cold for me, so just dipping my foot in was sufficient, but younger, more adventurous people would quickly dunk their full bodies.

There are numerous hike trail heads from the campground, giving a range of difficulties from a quick 20 minute walk to the hot spring to much longer hikes.  Silver falls is about 1.5 hour walk with great views of the falls and towering trees. Great place.

reviews.author: WILLIAM I.
reviews.text:
I was extremely disappointed to see that ALL of loop B has been closed to the tax paying public. It is now reserved for members of the Cowlitz tribe for ceremonies according to the rangers. 

I was further extremely disappointed to see several campsites in F loop closed to the public and held for National Park Service administration only. The site I had last year and was canceled out of two days before my trip because of hazardous tree was being used by, a friend  of a park service (?) while the hazardous tree remains! 

And of course, loop G remains closed for third year with only one tree down in one camp site. 

Several thief’s have taken place here also with folks loosing generators, prophane tanks, camp stoves and etc.

reviews.author: Don  B.
reviews.text:
Camp sites are poorly designed and maintained, length is substandard for size of RV”s and unleveled. Other then that
Campgrounds were clean and for the most part quiet

reviews.author: Jhoanna H.
reviews.text:
H016 was a fantastic site in a truly wonderful campground. It was big and spacious. Short walk to the bathrooms. Can see all of your neighbors through the trees but the big woods and space between H016 and other sites didn't make it feel "crowded" or invasive of privacy. We had 2 small tents, a hammock and still had a TON of space to run around and for the kids to play within our site. Bathrooms were dated but clean and stocked. Park Rangers made frequent rounds. There is a dish washing sink in a closet at the bathroom building (its a tiny little closet and what looks like a large rectangular "toilet" as my kids called it, but it served its purpose and it was really appreciated to have this sink area since the previous campgrounds we stayed at did not have anything at all). 

Lots to do near the campground. Saw people swimming down in the Ohanapecosh River below site C008 and also by the day use area in loop C. Silver Falls Loop Trail (2.7 miles/90 minutes) can be started and finished at loop B and an easy Hot Springs Nature Trail can be walked in about 20 minutes starting behind the visitor center and ending in Loop B.

No cell phone service in the campground (not until we got out near Packwood). 
No showers or laundry in the campground but can drive into Packwood RV campground for $5  showers, $5 laundry and $15 dump (no dumping on weekends) or drive 5 miles south of town to Cascade Peaks RV Park for $2 laundry, $3 showers, $8 dump station.
Can drive into Packwood for overpriced groceries and gas, as is usually the case in tourist towns (can't complain too much since having a grocery store 15 minutes away was appreciated).

Overall cannot recommend this campground enough. LOVED IT. And will be back again soon.

reviews.author: Akshay M.
reviews.text:
The campground was very nice and shady with a stream next to our campsite. The site was a
Little uneven but not too bad. Since the campground is on the eastern side of the park, there is lesser traffic compared to the more popular west entrances.

reviews.author: Ashlie R.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground!

reviews.author: Klaus B.
reviews.text:
Wonderful site close to the River. Hiked to Carter Falls - 45 min hike.
If traveling north, Chinook pass overlook is worth the detour.

reviews.author: Matt Y.
reviews.text: One of our favorite campgrounds! This site was next to a small creek which was very good for sleeping. This site was also very quiet and away from other campers giving it more of a secluded feel. During our stay we got to see them bring down a tree! It was really cool! This place is a must!

reviews.author: Josh J.
reviews.text: Campsite itself is great and pretty big. Small creek behind it that the kids were able to play in. Woke up one morning to my hatchet stolen, so we packed up and called the trip off. Campground itself typically feels safe, so this was a bit of a surprise. Will still be coming back, will just secure valuable items....

reviews.author: Josh J.
reviews.text: Considerable vehicle traffic and the fire pit is close to the road. Tent area is tucked away in the site but there is a considerable root in the middle of the tent area. Campground is still great and the rangers are awesome. Will be camping here again in a few weeks, just not at this campsite.

reviews.author: Tighe S.
reviews.text: Incredible....Don't miss the hike to the falls, and the drive to Paradise.

reviews.author: Daniel M.
reviews.text: Great campsite adjacent to creek, walking path, and restrooms. Bear box located on site. Vehicle space is limited and separated from remainder of campsite, so may not be appropriate for tents that affix to cars.

reviews.author: Boo Neng Y.
reviews.text: Really clean and tidy campsite

reviews.author: Emily F.
reviews.text: Awesome campground - wasn’t crowded at all, rangers were very kind, bathroom was clean, roads were clear, and the river was beautiful!

reviews.author: Noah B.
reviews.text: Best campsite ever!

reviews.author: Roberta d.
reviews.text:
End of season but we missed having the wood truck come by.  Your ranger nicely told us where we could buy some in Packwood.
An adjacent campsite was pretty obnoxious with a super bright light that extended at least five camp sites and that really sucked.  Not sure if there is anything you can do about that.  The restroom was easily the dirtiest that I EVER remember at a campground.  The sink had not been washed in forever.  The floor, swept, no I don't think so.  The male restroom apparently really stank, female's was ok.  All end of season but still a downer.  We still love the area so you get 4 stars.

reviews.author: April A.
reviews.text: Great private little site. The sewer lift came on around 830pm and wasn’t too loud.

reviews.author: Lawrence  N.
reviews.text: As always park is gorgeous.... but this site has a serious slant to park in. And the picnic table is up against the next site

reviews.author: Aida K.
reviews.text: We loved it ! Had a spot by the river and it was wonderful!

reviews.author: Cheri G.
reviews.text: Absolutely BEAUTIFUL!  Loved all of the scenery & hikes.  The campsite next to us had someone for OVER 14 days stay, very shady character who didn’t leave OR PAY beyond her 14 days while we were there….disturbing that she got away with that behavior. reviews.author: mark d.
reviews.text:
Great campground. Would really like to see the D loop stay open in September. Bathrooms were clean and functional
We will be back next season

reviews.author: Christian D.
reviews.text: Stayed two nights. Nice camp. Great location.

reviews.author: Guy H.
reviews.text: Great spot with reasonable distance both to Paradise and Sunrise. Only issue I can point out is that there was no place to wash dishes and it was unclear what the expected procedure is.

reviews.author: Andrew P.
reviews.text: Excellent walks and appropriate facilities in fantastic, natural, well managed areas.

reviews.author: Robert J.
reviews.text: We’ve been here many times and consider it one of our favorites. The riverside campsites are the best. The bathrooms (with running water) are always clean and stocked.

reviews.author: Julius W.
reviews.text: We head a great time at Ohanapecosh - toilets could be a bit cleaner but other than that it was great

reviews.author: Mardi W.
reviews.text: one of our favorite campgrounds.

reviews.author: DENNIS T.
reviews.text: The mice love it there

reviews.author: Steve C.
reviews.text: Fine campground, centrally located between Sunrise and Paradise. Enjoyed the falls loop trail locally, although it was a small disappointment that we couldn’t continue on to the Grove of the Patriarchs since the bridge to it collapsed a couple of years ago and hasn’t been repaired. Should also note that there is no functioning RV dump station at Ohanapecosh so plan accordingly.

reviews.author: Darren V.
reviews.text: Excellent campground! Has everything you can ask for! Even a cowboy twirling a lasso notifying every one of the upcoming show at the amphitheater. We took the 1.2 mile walk to Silver Falls and saw the Hot Spring along the way. It was quiet even with a bunch of younger kids next to us. We were able to take a short drive to Packwood to get some supplies and stop by the Brewery there. The only downside was not being able to have a campfire which is pretty much everywhere these days. Best place to camp!!

reviews.author: Paul P.
reviews.text: Within two days of our arrival the area received 1.05" rain yet no ground fires were allowed. The rest rooms were all uphill from the campsites - not great for 70 year-olds. The Silver Falls trail was reputed to be 2.7 miles but my Apple Watch calculated we walked over five miles. Staff at the visitor's center followed me around the store presumably to make it harder for me to shoplift. No concessions were available. Otherwise it was nice, LOL

reviews.author: Tabitha A.
reviews.text: Once again enjoyed the hike to Silver Falls. Camping at Ohanepecosh was peaceful.

reviews.author: Mohammed G.
reviews.text:
Being next to water was great. 
Very nice trails around.

reviews.author: Jennifer W.
reviews.text: beautiful, well kept campground, our kids (5 and 9 yo) had a blast and so did we.

reviews.author: Linda S.
reviews.text: Stayed in E7.  Nice area with lots of trees and good distance between sites. This site is quite narrow and requires stepping over roots and small logs. The only area for a tent is higher than the table and you must pass the fire ring on the way, which is also higher than the table. Think bi- or tri-level. With only one set of bathrooms/camping sink/spigots in the loop, we had to walk a bit to get there but it was clean.

reviews.author: James N.
reviews.text: Janet Jackson, the ranger, was personable and extremely helpful.

reviews.author: Susan S.
reviews.text:
Very easy check in. 
Current information about no camp fires and the week day road closures to Paradise would be great to have prominently displayed on your website.

reviews.author: Andres B.
reviews.text: Awesome location and facilities!

reviews.author: Jaehan P.
reviews.text: We had a great camping here. Very clean restroom and convenient trash and recycling station. The tent pad of our site was sloped and I had difficulty sleeping there.

reviews.author: Madeline C.
reviews.text: My boyfriend and I had a great stay, lots of strong douglas firs for hammocking! Not too buggy in late August when we went. The park rangers at the visitor's center were very helpful when we needed some last minute trail suggestions due to road closure. When Steven's Canyon road is open the campground is close to both Paradise and Sunrise. I was proposed to on the trail to First Burroughs in Sunrise. I will never forget this trip!

reviews.author: Jaehan P.
reviews.text: This is a good site. The tent pad area was flat and level. We really liked hiking on the left side of the Silver Falls trail.

reviews.author: Liv M.
reviews.text: We had a lovely experience by the side of the river. The sites saved for the day of arrival were very wonderful sites. There was lots of space between camp sites. Silver Falls was beautiful as always, a 1.2 mile hike to get there.

reviews.author: Joey B.
reviews.text: Amazing campground with large campsites all nestled in an old growth forest. The Ohanapecosh river was a brilliant blue-green & the hike to Silver Falls was very pleasant. I climbed to the very top of the falls before returning to camp. Only downside was the burn ban & lingering smoke; I get it. I’ll definitely be back with friends.

reviews.author: Craig D.
reviews.text: I never went. The smoke was unhealthy and I tried to cancel and get a refund but it was too late

reviews.author: craig s.
reviews.text:
Beautiful location, although heavily used.  Our campsite had no neighbors on either side, which added to the feeling of privacy.  Tent site and picnic table were in good shape.  Due to high fire danger, we were not permitted to use the fire ring.  Bathrooms were clean and modern, with a small closet for washing dishes.

We did not have time to attend the ranger programs or small museum, but they seemed nice. 

The nearby within-Park road to Paradise Visitor Center was closed Monday through Friday (apparently for construction).

reviews.author: Duncan M.
reviews.text: A very good time overall.  One recommendation would be to return the seats in the amphitheater and have Ranger programs there again.

reviews.author: Ian B.

reviews.author: lucas w.

reviews.text: First time at Ohanapecosh and loved it. Ended up extending repeatedly and stayed 12 days! Rangers were very helpful in accommodating my requests. I had guests come up on both included weekends and we all loved it. What a beautiful spot…in an old growth forest with a perfect clear and cold river running through. We did a lot of swimming and hiking. Site A054 was the only one available that would fit my 26 foot trailer. It is right by the bathroom so lots of foot traffic….met a lot of nice people!

reviews.author: Glenn A.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground, but noisy neighbors who played music on speakers until 1130pm

reviews.author: DARIN G.
reviews.text: The Rangers that were on site were very understanding of our concerns about campers who were disruptive and disregarding the rules that most campers were abiding by.  They, however, did not feel they had the authority to do anything to change the behavior of the campers who had been identified and complained about by many fellow campers.  The disruptions of the 4 tents, 3 cars and 20 or so very loud and rowdy campers in one campsite along with a dog that was left unattended and continuously barking for hours was unacceptable to us and many campers who were trying to enjoy a peaceful tent camping experience in our National Park system.   We decided to leave early because the stress and anxiety that was created because the park was not able to act in a way that protected my rights as a rule following member of society was excessive.  This was my only vacation this summer.  It was destroyed because the lawlessness that was allowed to continue created too much stress for me.  I am disappointed and regret my support of the National Parks.  It has lost its appeal for me as a destination for a nature lover, hiker, and tent camper.  I am 60 years old and have been supporting the National Park for over 20 years.

reviews.text: We've camped here for almost 20 years (2006 before the October flood damage) as a family and love it. We are sad how hard it has become to get a campsite. reviews.text: We've stayed here before, it's a very nice campground close to everything we were doing.  This time, however, they picked our spot for us instead of letting us self select.  We ended up in a spot we would not have ever chosen ourselves (there were many available that week day) and in hindsight should have tried to switch it.  Hard to do after you're all unloaded and tired & hungry!   Also this campground is quite large, and when we were there it was like a playground instead of a campground.  So many large groups playing music, kids running and screaming unsupervised, etc.  Don't come here expecting a peaceful outing.

reviews.author: Amerita  H.

reviews.text:
Good site for smaller group. While the site is large, you may struggle to find enough flat space for two tents. Check Google Maps Street View for better idea of what the campsite looks like. High tree cover. Creek is small. The campsite is below the road, and the driveway is on a slope.

Check when the campsite visitor center closes, for us it was 5pm. Silver Falls trail from the campsite is okay for a campsite trail, but I would rather spend the time doing Myrtle Falls or Narada Falls. There is no phone signal at the campsite, but full bars at Paradise if needed.

reviews.author: Max L.
reviews.text:
H7 is a great campsite. The campsite itself is on high ground, with forest to the back of the campsite, so it was private. Not sure about the campsite fitting two cars though, we could only fit one. The campsite can easily fit two large tents. High tree cover.

Check when the campsite visitor center closes, for us it was 5pm. Silver Falls trail from the campsite is okay for a campsite trail, but I would rather spend the time doing Myrtle Falls or Narada Falls. There is no phone signal at the campsite, but full bars at Paradise if needed.

reviews.author: Max L.
reviews.text:
Overall, C23 is a great campsite, unless you don't like white noise from a nearby large river, or if you are a group of more than 2 or 3 and sitting around a campfire watching the fire is important to you. Moderate tree cover. Check when the campsite visitor center closes, for us it was 5pm. Silver Falls trail from the campsite is okay for a campsite trail, but I would rather spend the time doing Myrtle Falls or Narada Falls. There is no phone signal at the campsite, but full bars at Paradise if needed.

Pros: The campsite is private. We managed to just about squeeze in two three-man tents. There is a large river running behind the campsite, and the white noise was a nice touch for us but may be too much for those who enjoy a quiet stay. Bathrooms in C loop were clean with soap and paper towels provided, though the soap ran out on the second day. There is a truck that drives around until ~7pm selling firewood for $7 a bunch, though I wouldn't rely on it 100%.

Cons: The fireplace grate was annoying. The fireplace grate is adjustable, massive and heavy duty. The grate entirely covers 50% of the campfire, while the other half is made up of thick rows of metal, providing ~50% visibility of the fire. The firepit under the grate is shallow but manageable. When the grate is up, it is big enough that you can not see over it if you are sitting, so there is only visibility from three quarters of the firepit. Remember the smoke will blow in one direction, so the three quarters easily becomes one half. If watching the campfire into the night is important to you and you have more than 2 or 3 people, this may not be the perfect campsite for you.

reviews.author: Dino C.
reviews.text:
Lovely campground.  We stayed at E005, in late July. Lots of trees and even underbrush. It made for a quiet experience, even though the campground was full.  E005 has room for a truck+trailer, or a couple cars. We squeezed 3 cars in, one night. 
Enough space for 2 tents spread apart, 3 tents if you're friendly.  The fire pit was good, a nice wide level area around it. We fit 7 chairs comfortably. Only a few mosquitos, and only at dusk. Just one of the people in our group got bit. 

The bathrooms are not far from the site, and they were well-maintained by the camp hosts. 

Easy access to the river, if you want to take a dip or a bath.  And there's a nice, easy 3-mile hike right from the campsite, to a scenic waterfall.  You can swim there, too. 

The campground is really close, like a 3 minute drive, to the east entrance (Stevens Canyon entrance) to Paradise. AFAIK, as of 2023 August, the road from that entrance to Paradise is still closed M-F for construction and maintenance. It's open on the weekends. 

We've previously stayed on the D loop, and the H loop.  All the sites seem to be very nice. I haven't had a bad experience. We really enjoy Ohanapecosh, and we'll return soon.

reviews.author: Angela W.
reviews.text: Great Campground. Clean, well maintained. Fire guy comes around every evening. Gorgeous swimming hole (icy water but lovely on an 80 degree day!)

reviews.author: Tristan S.
reviews.text: This is our second summer in a row Camping at Ohanapecosh. We usually like to try out new campgrounds, but this one is worth coming back to again and again. Such a beautiful place and so many things to do. I highly recommend this campground!

reviews.author: J.  B.
reviews.text: The rodent problem is out of control. No heads up from rangers either. We had mice in our rv crawling on us. In 200 nights camping the past couple years no animals ever. Tried lights and peppermint oil. They’re savvy critters at Ohanapecosh. Not all Site’s had bear boxes so what were you supposed to do with food - walk through another campsite every time you want something?. Rangers were generally uninformed about the park and surrounding areas. Visitor center is tired. Amphitheater disrepair is so sad. We’ve been to many NPs and State parks. This is one we’d never come back to. Ranier needs a reservation and parking pass system to help make a visit enjoyable.  It was like Disneyland on a mountain. At the GC, the crowds are big too, but they have it managed well.

reviews.author: Sarah M.
reviews.text: Ohanapecosh is a great campground. Very clean, quiet, and the rangers were very helpful when we needed assistance.

reviews.author: Therese G.
reviews.text: Na

reviews.author: Jean B.
reviews.text:
This beautiful campground is ideal for tents and small R.V.'s. 
The ranger in charge of camping was friendly, helpful, and flexible. 
Dom't expect much in the way of facilities at $20 a night ($10 Golden Age), but there was running water in the bathrooms and drinking water was available there also. Sites were almost all shaded by large trees. Generally, there was a large flat area around the table & bear locker. THe parking spaces were often less than 25 feet long, so laog trailers stay away!  The river below the bridge (in the middle of the campground) was spectacular - if potentially dangerous. Trail to Silver Falls is a must see.

reviews.author: Larry L.
reviews.text: Good location for access to both Sunrise and Paradise.

reviews.author: Sherman E.
reviews.text: We had originally reserved a campsite, but when we arrived, we wanted to learn whether there was another possibility.  The ranger was most accommodating and was able to do so for us.  The new campsite was excellent.  The bathrooms were clean, and our experience was delightful.

reviews.author: John-Luke S.
reviews.text: Beautiful scenery, clean bathrooms, helpful staff.

reviews.author: Corey S.
reviews.text: Very charming campground. I was initially trying to get into White River campground, but they were full. I'm actually a lot happier with Ohanapecosh than I think I would have been at White River. Two very different vibes. White River seemed a lot crunchier and Ohanapecosh seemed a lot more family friendly and cute. I could hear the river from my spot. The folks were very quiet except for the occasional burst of children's laughter as they ran past. Very clean. A wonderful place to be around other people, which is something I usually dread.

reviews.author: Susan  R.
reviews.text: Nice large campground, clean bathrooms. I would stick to the outer loops as the inner sites are not private. Overall a very nice campground with a swimming hole and hiking trails.

reviews.author: Phillip R.
reviews.text: Nice campground in beautiful location. Respectful group of campers. Close to many beautiful places.

reviews.author: Brian W.
reviews.text: Nice campground, with nice facilities. Also, has a ranger visitor center which was very helpful for gathering different information on hikes and sites to see. The only downside for our specific campsite, was the tent pad was very close to the campground road.

reviews.author: Loic J.
reviews.text: Amazing campground, so beautiful & the visitor was awesome!

reviews.author: Stephen  W.
reviews.text: We enjoyed our stay. There is a lot of construction and improvements going on. My biggest complaint is that the campground loops are one way going the wrong direction because van sliding doors open on the passenger side and sites were setup for access from the drivers side. Otherwise it was great. We got there and were able to get a FCFS site at 4 pm which was awesome!

reviews.author: David K.
reviews.text: We were so surprised to find that there were NO BUGS at our camp site. Not even in the evenings! We really liked staying on the H loop since it was more quiet than the other loops closer to the entrance. Would definitely stay here again!

reviews.author: Ryan O.
reviews.text:
This is a beautiful site right on the water BUT a path down to the most popular part of the river is literally right next to the fire pit. Enjoy 50-100 people walking through your campsite (even when at the top of the path there is nowhere to walk other than right through your campsite past your car because there are bushes that corral people in that direction) during the day and into early evening. 

It really is a nice site but this was very bothersome for us, but hey maybe your party won’t mind meeting some new people!

reviews.author: Amber E.
reviews.text: We tried to make reservations for anywhere in Washington or Oregon and everything was booked 6months out. We wanted to go somewhere else but realized too late it wasn’t first come/first serve. Luckily this campground does this and it was such a treat. They had a great visitor center which had loads of things for kids. There were trails and the pcr was not far off to access. Also the mount Rainer National park is nearby but extremely crowded. We didn’t do much of that because it was so busy. Worse than Disney crowds! As for the campground, the sites are nice, bear proof boxes for food. The fire pits don’t have rings which is the only negative thing I can say. Tiny rocks surround the pit. Which is strange since the fire rules are so strict. We had bikes with small kids, there is a great river running through the campground which was cold but refreshing. Very tidy!

reviews.author: Robert K.
reviews.text: Stayed in site A46. Adequate with flat spots for tent and picnic table with fire pit nearby. Nearest bathroom was okay but you had to walk through campsites to get to it. Nice nearby round trip hike to Sinver Falls.

reviews.author: Jeanne F.
reviews.text: The group site in A was spacious, with five tables and multiple fire pits that we used for cooking. We felt set back from the other campsites, which is perfect for a large group.

reviews.author: David B.
reviews.text: Great camping experience. Rangers were very helpful, campground was in great condition, and the Silver Falls hike from the campground was one of the best campground based hikes ever. Also allowed use to get to Sunrise early for a hike before the crowds. Loved it!

reviews.author: Ann T.
reviews.text: One of the best campgrounds in our state!  We've been coming here for many years and it never disappoints.

reviews.author: Charlotte D.
reviews.text: Wonderful campground! Beautiful sites and a quiet place to be. I loved easy access to hikes, but was a little let down by the hot springs - not soakable or tub-like, but very neat to walk to!

reviews.author: Brittany B.
reviews.text: We camped in H5. It was lovely and everyone was quiet and respectful. The only thing that was a bit odd bathrooms in the h loop are separated into male/female and the female bathroom has a urinal? Very strange.

reviews.author: Marcia  J.
reviews.text: We love Ohanapecosh! It’s incredible to camp among so many beautiful trees and the sparkling river. We’ve been visiting every summer for years and it’s always wonderful & safe.

reviews.text: Lots of mosquitoes and bugs!  Probably because a river is nearby.  Bears frequent the campground  - keep stuff in bear-box!  Can't get down to the river -  steep cliffs!  Bummer!

reviews.author: Marisa Claire M.
reviews.text: The Geology patio talk by Ranger Tom was a highlight for my kids, as were the jr ranger activities. Nice location within the park, clean family friendly campground, great places to hike and play without having to get back in the car.

reviews.author: Andy G.

Absolute peace and quiet..
No cell phone service to interrupt our family time.. will definitely be back soon.. this time we will NOT forget sleeping bags!

reviews.text: While I liked the campsite, area for text was about 15 feet from other campsites fire pit. Had a nice creek behind the site. Because it was so close to other campsite, I just slept in a hammock by the creek. Worked out well. Good site for tents, not sure about level ness for an RV

reviews.author: James G.
