reviews.text: Beautiful campground, very few bugs at this time. Higher elevations had tons of mosquitos! Dip in the Ohanapecosh River was refreshing!!! Overall clean restrooms and good water. Pretty quiet overall

reviews.author: Kelly M.
reviews.text: Arrived on a Tuesday at 10:30 am and was assigned A-44 for a first come, first serve site. Site A-44 was a wonderful site with room for my pop up trailer, room for at least two tents and trees for hammocks! Many other FF sites available but campground filled by the end of the week.

reviews.author: Christie S.
reviews.text: Very family friendly, individual bear boxes at site. Access to river for wading or swimming.  Site E016 is not properly mapped. It is right next to bathroom, very close to site E015 which is also on the same inner loop.

reviews.author: Keith P.
reviews.text:
A very beautiful place - but of course, it's Mt. Rainier National Park. 
The staff were friendly and helpful in the visitor center - which is very interesting on its own. For hikers, there are many beautiful trails, nicely groomed and for any level of hikers. The campsites were clean and enough space for our needs. As were are older people (but we tent camped on the ground), restrooms were conveniently placed, cleaned daily with running water. Just outside were hose bibs with clean, cold potable water.

Considering the "pay-for-everything" dynamic of today, $20/per night wasn't bad. My only less-than-satisfactory item was access to the river. In my younger years, I could've bounded down the hillside - but not at 68. Haha. 

All in all, it was a great experience as I took my wife (from Ukraine) camping for the first time in her life. She loved it and adapted as if she had done this her entire life. I would recommend this campground. Larger RVs will be difficult to navigate in some spots, but there are adequate spots for them.

reviews.author: elisabella t.
reviews.text: The campsite we got lucky with was perfect! We were not too close to the neighboring campsite

reviews.author: Elizabeth S.
reviews.text: The women working in the office were very helpful and knowledgeable when we were checking in. Camping in the NPS has become a nightmare in the last few years with all the regulations, and online reservations.

reviews.author: Scott W.
reviews.text: We had a great large area to camp and set up our pop up Coleman camper.  Very quiet and peaceful.  Great place to camp!

reviews.author: Alexander S.
reviews.text: Beautiful site with a great path down to the Ohanapecosh river. Tall trees are persistent through the entire campground and provide canopy coverage from the sun and light rain. The site next to ours was closed for administrative purposes, otherwise there likely would not have been enough privacy between the two sites as the firepit rings are located closer together. Highly recommend for small group camping.

reviews.author: William H.
reviews.text: Tiana was an awesome host!  We had the best night's sleep we've had in years next to the sound of the river.  Thank you Tiana for helping us and answering all our questions!  We will be back soon!

reviews.author: Jim K.
reviews.text: Great experience this year, quiet and great facilities

reviews.author: Jim K.
reviews.text: Campsites were clean and orderly.  Restrooms were also clean.  Our group had a great time even ere able to get up to Paradise over the 4th with the road being open for the Holiday.

reviews.author: David A.
reviews.text: Beautiful location near a beautiful river and large fits.  Very relaxing!

reviews.author: Chandler W.
reviews.text: There are some fun hikes and beautiful waterfall within hiking distance. There is a beautiful river running through the campground that you can swim in if you don't mind ice cold water. Specific to campsite E007, the campsite is horrible. Tripping and ankle-breaking hazards everywhere. The tent site was not as big as advertised and had a downed tree trunk sticking into it. The fire pit was not a pit at all which means your only walkway through your site is going to be a mudpit when you dowse your fire. Genuinely a very disappointing campsite in an otherwise pretty awesome campground.

reviews.author: Timothy S.
reviews.text: Please crack down on the weed smokers.

reviews.author: Danielle C.
reviews.text: Such a beautiful stay. Sites are a little closer than we are used too but so peaceful and definitely look forward to staying there again!!

reviews.author: Desire S.
reviews.text: Loved the location we camped at. Very close to the bathroom which was clean and had paper towels,TP, and hand soap. Not far from trash area and also close to the water station. The site is not super close to other sites either. Highly recommend H10! You can still hear the river and have the shade of the trees!

reviews.author: Tamara L.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground.  Nice little walk to Silver Falls. Understaffed this year.  So a little disorganized.

reviews.author: Elisabeth R.
reviews.text: Site is close to the river.  big enough - we had a 4 person tent.  a paved pad for the car.  fire pit. Perfect spot.  Listening to the river sound at night was soothing. Close enough to the bathrooms which are on the minimalist side - old sink and 4 stalls.  no shower facilities. We appreciated the bear-safe box for food storage.  The spot had a bit of sun which was great but also enough shade.  lots of mosquitoes on the 4th of July weekend.  We will be back.

reviews.author: Tessa R.
reviews.text: The campground is WONDERFUL - the ranger station is great and has really good programs for all ages (I have a 4 year old and she had a blast). We hiked to the hot springs and Silver Falls, both accessible from the campground, and they were perfect hikes for us. We are big fans of this campground and will definitely be coming back <3

reviews.author: Jennifer W.
reviews.text: Great campground! Easy access to lots of hiking trails and adventures. There are a lot of campsites crammed into a relatively small area so it’s definitely not very private or quiet, I wouldn’t choose this campground for relaxation. But it’s definitely a great place when I’m in the mood for exploration! I ended up leaving a day early because I had some neighbors that kept bumping their music loudly. It was kind of a bummer. I put noise canceling headphones on, but the base went right through them.

reviews.author: Yiling X.
reviews.text: Spacious site. Everything is good. I just wish there’s a bit more privacy. The neighbor is right next to our site. No trees or bushes in between. (If you have a big group, just book these two sites together then it will be great!

reviews.author: Susan P.
reviews.text: The campsite is beautiful and well maintained. There are nice hiking trails that begin right from  the campground. I like that it is quiet and not as busy as the other side of the park.

reviews.author: Kim A.
reviews.text: This is a great campground. Nicely spaced sites among the impressive trees. The rangers at the visitors center very helpful. Don’t miss the hike to Silver Falls—it  is terrific.

reviews.author: Tim E.
reviews.text: Wild green river, enormous trees very nice

reviews.author: Terri C.
reviews.text: Great location near Packwood and the Paradise entrance. Bathrooms were good. Some spots are more private than others.

reviews.author: Jenny L.
reviews.text: We stayed in loop H site 7 am last minute and it was an awesome site! One side was completely open to the forest and the other side had a site that was more than enough distance away. Clean facilities. Zero cell service for us, so plan your next day hikes ahead of time : )

reviews.author: Grayson F.
reviews.text: Wish there was a shower or wash room

reviews.author: Lynn H.
reviews.text: Great campground. Shady. A nice trail to falls from campground. I love that they have first come sites.  Thanks

reviews.author: Michael P.
reviews.text: The Staff was exceptional. We shifted a reservation, as we did not want to move from a FCFS site. The Rangers also provided pertinent park information and highlighted a number of hikes, especially for my wife who suffers limited mobility. The campground is clean and well managed. The setting along the Ohanapecosh River pleased my wife greatly. Ohana is conveniently located between between Sunrise and Paradise.

reviews.author: Stuart F.
reviews.text: This was a campground that was beautiful, but the visitor center was closed.  Also, there are no showers here, so that stinks.  Finally, due to road work, most of the park was inaccessible.  But the campground was spacious and beautifully located within an old growth forest.  We also were able to go on a fun short hike near the campground.

reviews.author: Harpreet B.
reviews.text: Campsite was great with beautiful view of the river. Staff was friendly and informative, and restrooms were clean.

reviews.author: Nick K.
reviews.text:
Great campground, great vibes, very scenic, lots of cool stuff to do (hiking trails etc), toilets well maintained with good-sized sites and friendly rangers. 
Only gripe is we only stayed one night, got in late and left early-ish (~9am) so we didn’t get to go to the visitor centre which looked very interesting :( unfortunately we were road tripping from Seattle to Los Angeles and we had a schedule to keep.

reviews.author: Ronald C.
reviews.text: Nice campground with access to fun on the river and trailhead to Silver Falls. Loop C is a super busy loop. Expect people to walk through your site to get to/from the river if your site is along it. The same goes for campsites around the restroom. The campsites in Loop C are pretty tight. C006 and C007 are best if reserved together. Same goes for sites C010 and C011. C008 has a back-in angle that is counterintuitive to the one-way loop. Recommend going around the loop and then backing into site C008 from the opposite direction. A path from the river leads up to site C008 so uninformed people might walk through campsite to exit the river.

reviews.author: Rebecca M.
reviews.text: Lovely forest with some easy hikes right from the campground. Sites were packed in a bit tightly. CCC era restrooms were relatively clean for their age. Some recycling facilities were available. Unfortunately more than half the sites in the campground were closed when we were there leading to artificial scarcity and a packed campground.

reviews.author: Claudio G.
reviews.text: Similar to C30. Good but there are better spots along the river

reviews.author: Claudio G.
reviews.text: Not the greatest section. Try to get something closer to the river if you can

reviews.author: Claudio G.
reviews.text: Perfect view

reviews.author: Christopher J.
reviews.text: A good stay. Five days, four nights. Booked back in February. With La Wis Wis closed this season, my choices were super slim. In hindsight, only A, B, and C loops were open at Ohanapecosh. Grounds crews sawed up fallen trees across the bridge. I waited around for the firewood guy, but gave up on him. Went into Packwood three times, for a total bundle count of 23 bundles. Early June is chilly, 40-50⁰ at night. Not much animal sightings. A couple chipmunks, a crow, two camp robber birds, a robbin, and a finch. There are bear boxes here, so bears do exist. Flushing toilets, and running water sinks. No showers. No campground hosts, but a Visitor Center, with actual Park Ranger, junior ranger uniform staff. Very friendly.

reviews.author: Lei G.
reviews.text: Pretty big lot, beautiful trail nearby.

reviews.author: Robert M.
reviews.text: The campsite is located in a tranquil old growth douglas fir forest. Stunning trees and a short hike to a dramatic waterfall.

reviews.author: Cassandra C.
reviews.text: Had a beautiful quiet site near the creek. Great nature getaway!

reviews.author: Jennifer F.
reviews.text: Perfect trip

reviews.author: Chris H.
reviews.text: Beautiful, heavily wooded campground with great hikes starting from there. Don’t miss Silver Falls! The park staff was super nice and helpful . Do be aware that despite the listed lengths for sites, it may be very difficult, if not impossible, to back your rig in. I had to swap out sites. Loop A has more larger and easier to maneuver sites than C.

reviews.author: Ed R.
reviews.text:
Disappointed that the visitor's center was still not open  a week after Memorial Day. It's alwasy a nice part of our expeience over the seven years in a row that we have been there. Please find a way to gather enough staff in the future. We need our parks running well.

Also the staff person at the window had no valuabble info, and acted disinterested. It was a young lady.

reviews.author: Michelle D.
reviews.text: Our campsite was surrounded by RVs with generators going off most of our stay.  Not the best choice when you have a tent and want to enjoy the view.  The hike to the waterfall and the easy access to the river from the campsite was great.

reviews.author: Shunfan D.
reviews.text: C1 is a bit smaller than the other campsites in C loop, but we had no problem setting up three tents there. I had a nice three-mile run around all the loops and really enjoyed hiking on the silver falls trail. The campsite is close to the river, which is a bonus, and it gets good sun exposure.

reviews.author: Dmitry V.
reviews.text: Amazing campground along the river. Hiking trail access from the campground. Can’t miss.

reviews.author: Bernhard E.
reviews.text: Very nice and very quiet place

reviews.author: Tasha S.
reviews.text:
Site D6 is close to the river, but completely open to site D5. Next time I would want to reserve both sites to have someone I know next to me. This site is close to a STEEP river trail that leads down to a nice quiet spot to relax. If you can navigate the trail, you have a nice little private beach of your own to read a book and catch the last sun spots of the day.

I love this campground because of how close it is to many trails. At times the campground is quite loud...and many of the spots are not private. But, I am on a mission to find a list of the campsites at Ohanapecosh that feel private (to me)...because the area is just so beautiful and amazing. 

This drawback of this campground, like many I went to this summer...is that there were SO MANY empty spots that said reserved. I saw many spots that I would have LIKED to camp in...but they were reserved and NOBODY showed up. So sad that other humans are doing this. It's not that hard to cancel a reservation online. I mean, if you aren't gonna camp...cancel and release your campsite for others to experience the beauty and mental health benefits of being immersed in the outdoors.

reviews.author: Russ P.
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful campgrounds we have experienced, even with most of the loops being closed either for the season or because of tree-falling danger.  Hiking options directly from the campsite are a bit limited, but many trailheads are accessible with a short drive.  Access to the Grove of The Patriarchs is closed because the bridge is out, but you'll still be awed by the scenery.  Site and facilities are clean, campsites are fairly large and bear boxes for everyone!  We'll be back.

reviews.author: Glen U.
reviews.text: Site A-22 is really great. The smoke was rather horribly bad but that is not the fault of NP service.

reviews.author: Gregory H.
reviews.text: An excellent camping experience with incredible views, sounds, and scents.

reviews.author: Nicholas M.
reviews.text: Campground is well maintained and the rangers are very professional and helpful. Ohanapecosh is a beautiful setting.

reviews.author: Michelle D.
reviews.text: Nice hike right in the campsite, close to many other great hikes, beautiful trees, campsites overlooking the river. Great location for visiting all Mt Rainier has to offer.

reviews.author: scott c.
reviews.text: We spent 5 nights there in Loop C after the regular season during the 'First-Come First-Serve' time. The rangers were wonderful and helpful. The hiking is fun and the river is a treasure. The facilities are old and tired the the maintenance was minimal.  By Friday the open loops were pretty full though it was fairly quiet during the week.

reviews.author: Richard B.
reviews.text:
What a perfect weekend to end the season. We have camped at Ohanapecosh in all types of weather but never as perfect as this past weekend.  Hopefully the Stevens Canyon road to Paradise will soon be opened.  
Ohanapecosh remains one of the nicest campground within the National Parks we have visited.

reviews.author: Jennifer F.
reviews.text: We love it here

reviews.author: Kathryn G.
reviews.text: Lovely campground. Rangers placed us in a double site and then added another group with their dog even though other spaces were available. We got relocated. Check out the hot springs

reviews.author: Anne K.
reviews.text:
The staff was very helpful and friendly.  Only issue was a sullen young man had a large German Shepard on the waterfall trail.  The dog lunged at me. The dog’s leash was dragging on the ground. The guy said it was an emotional support dog.

A BMW driving woman took her golden retriever into the women’s restroom.  No one else could enter until they were done.

reviews.author: Jeffrey H.
reviews.text: We went off season, so we appreciated the quiet.

reviews.author: Jerry  C.
reviews.text: The young staff was so nice. The best I’ve been around since camping there for the last 20 + years

reviews.author: David F.
reviews.text: Late in season so not crowded. Beautiful weather and friendly rangers.

reviews.author: Susan L.
reviews.text: We are from Michigan but have stayed on the C loop of Ohanapecosh at least three or four times now.  We just love how the campsites back up to the river.  The Silver Falls trail right at the campsite is a wonderful loop leading up to the falls, and then circling around to return.  It is longer than the sign indicated, closer to four miles round trip, not just over two as we had thought, but awesome trail.

reviews.author: Bonnie P.
reviews.text: Nice gravel site in old growth timber.   A bit far to bathroom and water.  We were lucky to have bushes on the east, a stream on the north and an empty spot on the west.

reviews.author: Brett L.
reviews.text: As an out of state visitor we were surprised with the State fees on everything.  Also there were very few common ammenities one would expect in a national park.  No wifi available at the visitors center, dump station has been removed (buried), bathrooms are old and need updating along with the potable water can be along way from campsites.  On the positive side, the location and scenery are spectacular.  We will be back in the area sometime, but will probably not stay in this campsite again.

reviews.author: Niall C.
reviews.text: Great campsite. Hike to the falls, it's really worth it. Helpful Rangers.

reviews.author: Richard S.
reviews.text: Great time of year at Mt Rainier!

reviews.author: Brandy B.
reviews.text:
The park was beautiful!
Made the hike up to silver falls . Amazing!!
Reasonably priced too!

reviews.author: Frank D.
reviews.text: Big sites with lots of flat space close to a river.  In early Sep. all the sites across the river were closed but the sites in the A, B, and C loop were full. Only one bathroom for each loop and they were very old and needed an update. Nice hike to Silver Falls.

reviews.author: Floris M.
reviews.text: The staff was wonderful and the campground gorgeous.  The only problem was the reservation people put "first come first serve" on all the campsites in sections D.E, F. H so everyone who had a reservation up to Sept 6 assumed they could stay as first come first serve.   Actually the park closed all those sections and people got up at 6 am to stand in line to get a place at the park for the Sept 7th on.  The staff even handled that well, but there was no excuse for the reservation problem.  All they needed to do was code the closed sections, unavailable.

reviews.author: Jenny G.
reviews.text: Amazing campsite! Clean restrooms, flat sites and a spectacular hike to a waterfall right from the campgrounds--truly perfect!

reviews.author: Jessica  C.
reviews.text: They closed the area of the campground we were staying in without notice and did not inform us it was closed until all the other campsites were sold out. They were unwilling to accommodate. So we had to drive 3 hours back home.

reviews.author: Jamie S.
reviews.text: Ohanapecosh campground is our families favorite campsite! We try to visit at least once a year. This year, the weather was the best any of us has seen! It was amazing. The scenery is breathtaking, the facilities are always clean and stocked, the walks/hikes are memorable, and the campground always seems to be having something going on for our kids to enjoy! I couldn't say one negative thing.

reviews.author: abigail k.
reviews.text: Great site and campground. Campground vibe was super quiet and respectful, mainly families. A little bit close to the neighbors on one side, but not a big deal. Bear locker at this site was broken.

reviews.author: Weizu L.
reviews.text: Excellent camping site. Very enjoy the stay.

reviews.author: James N.
reviews.text: I was so happy this was not a strictly reservation only campground, but first arrivals like me were allowed. Thank you. This allows for freedom for US citizens to travel. Too many people are unable to follow through with trip plans. Woman checking me in was friendly and helpful. Campground itself was very nicely designed and laid out, was nice to be by a small stream. Tall trees were wonderful! Having flush toilets in a campground was a pleasant surprise. The trail to Silver Falls was nice. Was great to have recycling bins right in the campground. I would recommend this campground to friends and family.

reviews.author: Brea N.
reviews.text: Lots of fun!  Great hiking close by.

reviews.author: David J.
reviews.text: A beautiful spot, conveniently located to both Sunrise and Paradise.

reviews.author: Bruce B.
reviews.text: The campground is beautiful, campsites are well spaced.  Signage is great, would love to come back again.

reviews.author: Danielle D.
reviews.text:
Best bathrooms, polite campers. 
My favorite campground ever.

reviews.author: Katherine A.
reviews.text: The campsites were big, the bathrooms clean, and the hiking and scenery was beautiful! We had the absolute best time!!

reviews.author: Gillian V.
reviews.text: nicely wooded, lots of shade, decent campsite space, but tent area not level. Excellent firepit. Solution for dumping dishwater in toilets totally impractical. Beautiful river with swimming possibility if you can stand cold water.

reviews.author: Vibhor G.
reviews.text: Excellent campground location with clean facilities.

reviews.author: Giri V.
reviews.text: Love this camp ground. Clean and amazing beauty all around. The rangers are really helpful and awesome.

reviews.author: Joan B.
reviews.text: This is such a beautiful quiet campground with ready access to amazing trails.  Absolutely loved this campground!

reviews.author: Ferenc K.
reviews.text: My favorite campsite, has a unique feeling camping under these giant trees

reviews.author: Lisa  H.
reviews.text: Ohanapecosh is always fantastic. I was so disappointed at how many camper just didnt show up for their reservations.  I spent hours and hours trying to get reservations back in February, and I could have just walked in last minute and gotten a site! I hope you are considering changes in how no shows are handled. Just losing the per nite fee is not enough! $20-60 bucks is a drop in the bucket to many. Its not the families and experienced campers who are taking advantage of the system. Your staff  is always the best I have interacted with! Thank you for what you do. I wish people in general were more thoughtful and appreciative of this wonderful place.

reviews.author: Eryn B.
reviews.text: We loved the big trees that provided plenty of shade, and the creek that ran through the campground was a great place to cool down!

reviews.author: Debra B.
reviews.text: Thanks for such a good experience

reviews.author: David C.
reviews.text: This campground is different than most others I have visited. Upon arrival if you do not have reservations you are supposed to go to the rangers office and pay for a site. If you have an RV they do not have a place for you to park to go to the office and they had no signs saying check in first. I wound up parking in a site that had no reserved sign on it and then hiking to the rangers office to make my single night purchase. When I was purchasing my site they said I need to come to them before occupying it kind of passive aggressively. Other than that the campground was clean and beautiful. The visitors center was pretty neat and I would visit again if the opportunity arises.

reviews.author: Amy R.
reviews.text: Crowded and campsites small. Not pet friendly.

reviews.author: Casey D.
reviews.text: Very family friendly and accessable. The river access and trails where both tons of fun. The visitor center staff where incredibly informative and helpful!!

reviews.author: Ben F.
reviews.text: Nice hiking opportunities. No mosquitoes. Clean campground.

reviews.author: DHAWAL O.
reviews.text: Great campground.  Toilets (H loop) could be a tad better.  One of the toilets in the women's restroom had a peculiar shape that I have never seen and it didn't even have a seat.  So only one stall in the women's restroom was usable.

reviews.author: mothana a.
reviews.text: It is very good and nice

reviews.author: Nolene S.
reviews.text: This is a lovely location.  Not overly busy.  Great sites.

reviews.author: Marne T.
reviews.text:
Couldn't be better. Rangers were all friendly and campsites clean and bathrooms great. Silver falls was a delight and my husband even swam down below where they were fishing even though no fish caught that day.
My only complaint was when I tried to get 2 days on the website, it only gave me one and when I went back on, the second night was gone. I guess I was too slow and others grabbed it.
Looking forward to the Grove of the Patriarchs when we return next year or later.

reviews.author: Paul S.
reviews.text:
We stayed in the A loop next to the bathrooms. It would be nice to get the lights to project more on the ground. I work for Redwood National Park and we changed the outdoor lighting at facilities to special night lighting that maintains both dark skies and does not attract insects. 

The bathroom fixtures need to be updated as the faucets were loose. I do like the fire pits being up on a concrete pad where there is better air. I know air inversion is a problem so check on some YouTube videos about creating a fire pit that is smokeless. It exists. 

The path to the swimming area needs to be fixed. There is too much erosion going on so a walkway down to the river bar and revegetating the area would be in order. 

Please keep some sights first come, first served as there are still people who travel this way. It seems to me that since the park is so popular and all the campgrounds only allow smaller campers and trailers that another campground needs to be considered maybe near Longmire so it can be on the same water system. The sights could then accommodate large RV’s and trailers. 

Thank you for good roads in the park, if only you could get Washington to work on their roads. 

Finally, at Cougar Rock campground, the wash basin for kitchen items is very nice. Maybe the same should be made at Ohanapecosh.

reviews.author: Steve L.

reviews.text: Love it there

reviews.text: We love this place. quite ,dog friendly, will go back again

reviews.text:
Preimier site, at a premier campground, in a world class National Park. 
Clean, friendly, safe, absolutely gorgeous.

reviews.author: William S.
reviews.text:
Site by the river was outstanding.
The ranger Taylor S was helpful and very knowledgeable.

reviews.author: Uyen N.
reviews.text: It is a beautiful campground to relax and unplug from the busy world.

reviews.author: Melissa D.
reviews.text: This is our favorite campground, and our destination for a family camping trip for the last 17 summers.  The last few years have been challenging to book - from hazard trees during the pandemic to entire loops going FCFS - we miss the "ease" of the old days.  This year we chose to wake up and drive to the campground - arriving at 7:30am - to hopefully book sites.  We were successful (hooray!), and then drove home to pack up the truck to return later that afternoon.  We love this place, and would do the FCFS again - but it adds a layer of stress and uncertainty that feels contrary to the relaxing experience we are seeking. We are hopeful that the entire campground will return to a reservation system again for next season (and forever).

reviews.author: Dhani C.
reviews.text: The sites are large and beautiful. It was a short walk to water and there was so much to do. Many trails are right in the campground so you don’t have to drive.

reviews.author: Jeanne C.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground, but site C7 was awful. It is right next to a path down to the water, so all day long people walked right through our site to get to the river. They came in droves, dragging their strollers, dogs, coolers, etc. right through our campfire circle without even a “sorry”. It was obnoxious. Site C6 is supposedly a separate site, but the way the sites are designed their campfire was practically on top of ours. I would not ever book this site again. What a disappointment.

reviews.author: Ingrid O.
reviews.text: Beautyfull place, I recommend

reviews.author: soohee L.
reviews.text: Great

reviews.author: Adam H.
reviews.text: Come ready for anything. There is cold water to swim in! Beautiful location close to the park.

reviews.author: Sachin U.
reviews.text: Easy to find. Wish there were more rounds of firewood. Restrooms were clean

reviews.author: Anna L.
reviews.text: I have camped at Ohanapecosh for 64 years I always try to spend my birthday there and was able to do that this year with my grandchildren what I love the most there is the trees have been there since my grandparents used to come to the Hot Springs resort back in the 30s and 40s when they bring my mom and her sister camping there and my mom brought us I brought my kids and now I bring my grandchildren so for five generations the same trees are there. Staff was helpful exhibit at the visitor center are wonderful and still there and we really enjoyed going up to Paradise and Box Canyon. Thank you for being good stewards of the park I hope it will be there for my grandchildren’s children!

reviews.author: Sierra L.
reviews.text: We stayed during the week with two kiddos (3 and 8) in the H Loop. Everything was easy to access, clean, and everyone was friendly. The visitors center is a great place to start when planning any Hiking in the area. There are no showers to make sure you are prepared with other ways to stay clean. We also loved that there were safety bins to store our food to protect it from animals.

reviews.author: Eric D.
reviews.text: Thank you.

reviews.author: Catherine L.
reviews.text: Perfect location. Beautiful campsite .

reviews.author: Cornelia H.
reviews.text: The campground was beautiful but the sanitairy facilities wäre not well maintained.

reviews.author: Ellen D.
reviews.text: Although this campground doesn't offer a lot of privacy the grounds are nicely kept. We had close river access, which was amazing. Love the area and proximity to Rainier and so many trails.

reviews.author: Anna A.
reviews.text:
Upon arrival, the information center has clear instructions for reservation holders. The sites are well kept, clean, and spacious. Bear boxes are provided for food storage. The bathrooms were clean and had lights. 
The river is gorgeous and there is a beach and a rock for jumping into the bracingly cold water! Within the park is a wonderful trailhead for Silver Falls. It's an easy 2.7 mile hike and the payoff is a raging waterfall view. There is an additional short path to the rocks by the falls.  Gorgeous! I want to go back ASAP!

reviews.author: Yann M.
reviews.text: Perfect location for activities on the East side of the mountain. Great camping in the trees. Good access for local hikes right out of the campground.

reviews.author: Audrey G.
reviews.text: This campground is beautiful. We only had a short stay, but it was very clean and quiet.

reviews.author: Michele L.
reviews.text: We were lucky enough to get a somewhat isolated spot in Loop E and enjoyed the quiet atmosphere and lovely forest location.  We had a swim in the river - cold!!! and hiked the trails.  The rangers were kind and helpful.  We were very sad that Loop G was closed due to hazard trees as those campsites are favorites of ours.

reviews.author: Liv M.
reviews.text: We were not able to reserve a site until a couple of days before our trip. It was a lovely site. There seems to be more spaciousness around sites than in years past. Everyone was friendly and relaxed. Thanks so much for doing what you can do to keep up the grounds with less budget.

reviews.author: Lara N.
reviews.text: What a great campground. Well maintained and great camping experience with friendly rangers and beautiful surroundings. We will be back for sure.

reviews.author: Camryn W.
reviews.text: loved that there were trails at the campsite and places to cliff jump and swim in the river. there were so many people in the water which was so fun to watch! good accessibility to the river bank as well if you just want to hangout and not swim. has a visitor center which is great and fire wood for sale too. lovely!

reviews.text: One of the coolest campgrounds around!

reviews.text: A great time every time, the shade towering trees and sounds of the rapids are as peaceful as you could ever want. The last several times we’ve been there it was during a heat wave jumping in the river midday was almost a necessity. It’s a classic representation of a national park campground.

reviews.author: Laci R.
reviews.text: Incredible campground. Clean bathrooms. Great hikes near the campground.  Beautiful swimming holes to cool off in. Couldn’t have had a better experience in this breathtaking park.

reviews.author: George A.
reviews.text: Good sites, access to hiking, and ice cold laughing water creek to cool off

reviews.author: Flannery J.
reviews.text: Gorgeous old-growth forest.

reviews.author: Rebecca D.
reviews.text: So many lovely trails to venture out to from this campground - also was thankful for the day use spots next to the river for some wading on an extremely hot day. So beautiful!

reviews.author: Shawn G.
reviews.text: Get reservations! Beautiful place, lots of space, and great people.

reviews.author: Patrick F.
reviews.text: We were walk-ins and the Park staff were most helpful and friendly

reviews.author: paul g.
reviews.text: I had the best campsite i'very ever had! Privacy from neighboring sites, 25 ft from bath house and Visitor Center and quiet at night. And incredible old growth conifers . Wow

reviews.author: Colleen B.
reviews.text: So quiet, calm and lovely.

reviews.author: Dorothy  H.
reviews.text: Great Campground, site C 15 overlooking the beautiful Ohanapecosh River was large and awesome!   Only con is that the sites in the campground offer very little, if any, privacy.

reviews.author: Matthew G.
reviews.text: Fantastic place to camp! The hike to silver falls was awesome, and perhaps do yourself a favor and take the long way around. It's a little more work but worth it.

reviews.author: Philo F.
reviews.text: The national park has no dump stations?  They have a sophisticated sewer system in the Ohanapecosh campground complete with flush toilets and sewer stations and pumps but no place for RV's to dump.  They are also sadly lacking in camper support facilities like a camp store.  On Wednesday and Thursday the concessionaire is closed at the Sunrise visitor center location?  No place to buy anything like water or snacks for a hike.  Kudos to the park for rebuilding their roads.  Trails were in good condition.

reviews.author: Scott T.
reviews.text: Very little site privacy. Restroom cleaning and resupply sorely lacking.

reviews.author: Cristobal S.
reviews.text: Close to the neighboring campsite. Nice area to camp with kids.

reviews.author: Ngoc N.
reviews.text: Lovely campground with lots of trees, clean bathroom. However we stayed at campsite H004, it’s super tiny and literally it’s just few steps away from other campsite. We can hear all conversation the whole time 😩 we didn’t enjoy the stay here

reviews.author: Prad R.
reviews.text: Large campsite with hikes to creeks and falls. Clean and well maintained.

reviews.author: Rolf W.
reviews.text: Nice placr

reviews.author: David F.
reviews.text: We had two different sites and both where excellent. Weather was good and we enjoyed many hikes.

reviews.author: Stephanie U.
reviews.text: Just lovely campground. Stargazing isn’t as good as you’d hope.

reviews.author: Francis B.
reviews.text: We lived this campground.  Very peaceful and good hiking nearby.  Restrooms were kept up nicely and the nightly delivery of firewood by the local firewood guy was a nice touch.  We would definitely stay here again.

reviews.author: Gaurab C.
reviews.text: One of the best. 5*

reviews.author: Carly Y.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground. Silver Falls hike was a great afternoon activity and the water is pristine. The nearby town (Packwood) was a great spot to buy some firewood and coffee.

reviews.author: Vicki C.
reviews.text: We love this campground. It is quiet and sheltered in the old growth forest. It is convenient to both the Sunrise and Paradise sides of the park. Within the campground itself are a well staffed Visitor Center and trailheads for a nature trail and beautiful Silver Falls. The Ohanapecosh River runs through the campground and provides sweet rushing water white noise at night. The staff and campground host are amazing.  So why not 5 stars??? Because your chances of finding paper towels in a rest room seem to be less than 10%. We were there for over a week, so this wasn't a fluke or an end of the weekend thing.  So go and enjoy a wonderful, peaceful experience. Just bring your own hand towel.

reviews.author: Tom J.
reviews.text:
I was in a 24’ motorhome.    Site H-002
- One entire loop was closed because of signs about root rot and perceived risk.   Same with a few sites scattered throughout the CG.  Yet, people are allowed to assume risk by walking on trails.   One cannot manage the area “so that nothing bad ever happens.”
- This is a dedicated campground and not wilderness.   Accordingly, the NPS should “surface log” all of the downed and fallen timber.   It can and does interfere with site access.  
- The online site descriptions are not a reliable means of determining whether one’s RV will fit in any particular site.  Because of the fallen timber mentioned above and the slope of the site, I was forced to do some creative blocking to approximately level my RV.  
-

reviews.author: Michael J.
reviews.text: I spoke at length with the park manager about my observations.  The amount of unauthorized parking of vehicles in the campground made it very unsafe, especially for campers and  their children.  I observed two children who were almost struck by unauthorized vehicles.

reviews.author: Jayne R.
reviews.text: Site C22 is listed as "waterfront" with two tent pads but it is NOT. It's in the center of a loop with no privacy and no tent pads. I tried to add the vacant site next to mine but the staff person said it was booked, but it wasn't.

reviews.author: Andrew C.
reviews.text:
The rangers were really helpful in suggesting hikes and providing information about the park. 
My original reservation was for 4 nights but decided to stay 6, and a ranger helped me get a first come first serve site. Very nice campground, thank you!

reviews.author: Kerry K.
reviews.text:
Awesome!
Great experience for the entire family.

reviews.author: Bridget F.
reviews.text: We have camped here for nearly a decade and love coming back every year. The rangers are so friendly and knowledgeable. The ranger class is always great!

reviews.author: Ashley S.
reviews.text: Our site at Ohanapecosh campground was absolutely beautiful. Towering mossy trees surrounded the site and aquamarine colored river ran next to us, which was very soothing for sleep. Site was well equipped with concrete picnic table and fire circle. Bathrooms were clean and easily accessible with fresh water available as well. Ohanapecosh provided easy access to the short hot spring trail, and the silver falls trail. The falls were stunning, lots of power. Definitely an experience I would suggest!

reviews.author: Matt Y.
reviews.text: Great site! The silver falls trail runs behind it so be prepared to see people behind the campsite and E8 is really close to this site.

reviews.author: Shannon W.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground! Nice east hike to an amazing waterfall.

reviews.author: Maura C.
reviews.text:
What a gem of a campground and an even better campsite.
A21 is set by itself on high ground. A short downhill walk to the river. Falling asleep to the sounds of the river. Check. Waking up to the sounds of the river. Check. The driveway can be tricky for backing in and leaving (might take a couple reracks). Overall amazing site, beautiful view. Guy sells wood for $7 a bundle and it includes some kindling. He shows up later in the day and makes 2 pass through. I wish he had a bell of some sort to alert us he is driving through. We missed him a couple times.

reviews.author: Aaron G.
reviews.text: We had prepared our eager 7&10 year olds for an educational, interactive Ntl. park experience similar to ours in the past. We expected presentations by rangers, group hikes, etc. but the ampitheater was deconstructed and there were no evening activities. The falls loop was a great hike for families with kids leaving from the campground. The facilities were getting run down, one bathroom was closed due to a broken septic pipe and the backup bathroom had a leaky sink pipe with an overflowing 5 gal bucket catching the drips. Bathrooms were unclean and smelled strong. Firewood was overpriced ($7 for 4-5 small pieces). Beautiful, quiet and cool on a hot day under old growth trees.

reviews.author: John R.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsite near the river. Only downside was the numbskulls playing loud music… sigh.

reviews.author: Rajiv D.
reviews.text: We really like the campground. The rest rooms were clean and well-maintained.

reviews.author: Beth Z.
reviews.text:
I needed to cancel my 2 night reservation within a day of arrival.  It was impossible to figure out how to cancel via the website and when I searched for the ranger station's phone number, Google listed the incorrect phone number and I was never able to get in touch to cancel my site.  Sadly, this probably meant at least one night this site went used.  Hopefully someone was able to use it the second night of our reservation as demand for camping is high.
Please include the ranger station's phone number on the email confirmation sent a few days before arrival.

reviews.author: Daina H.
reviews.text: The beautiful setting with the huge trees and the color of the Ohanapecosh River are very relaxing.  There are plenty of trails to wander on and nearby Mt. Rainier National Park to visit.  Well used park as it has been used for 100 yrs or so.

reviews.author: Colleen D.
reviews.text: Huge campground near the Ohanapecosh River in Mount Rainier National Park.  There are several trail options that start from the campground and all are great for families. You can visit the little hot springs (these are not big enough to bathe in) to enjoy the colors and flowers and the gorgeous Silver Falls is just about a mile from the campground visitor center.  The rangers are super fun and helpful, the bathrooms are very well maintained and we always have a great time while we're there!

reviews.author: WILLIAM I.
reviews.text:
I find it totally unacceptable that all of G loop, along with several campsites closed due to hazardous trees. The tree access ent needs to be done, completely, then immediately those effected trees need to be cut down to eliminate site closures!! In add, the limbs need to be chipped up. Limbs all over make the campground look very raty and unkept. 
When a person logs in to make a reservation, as soon as he starts to enter data on a site, that site should be locked up for him to complete his entry. When I started to make mine , as it was shown to be available, before I could finish someone else was given the site. That is totally unfair. I lost the site because I can’t type and have to peck.

reviews.author: Elma H.
reviews.text: Great site overlooking the river. Was able to fit one 4 person tent with room remaining. A short walk to the bathrooms. This site has no neighbors on either side just across from it.

reviews.author: Stephen B.
reviews.text: Quiet, incredibly beautiful campground.  The 3 mile hike to Silver Falls is easy and amazing.

reviews.author: Cheryl F.
reviews.text:
Loved our campsite here! We were in F14, and had plenty of room for our 28’ Class C and our car! 
Did several hikes from the CG, and they were awesome…the loop hike to the Falls was awesome! 
Also went up to Sunrise…the snow was still heavy on July 2nd, so I didn’t get to do the hikes to Frozen Lake and up on the Ridge, but I loved my time at this CG!

reviews.author: Megan R.
reviews.text: trailheads for the silver falls loop directly from campground is a definite highlight

reviews.author: Carolyn F.
reviews.text: Big sites with privacy.  Many sites are along a creek or river, or the river is audible from the site.  Some sites also back to the forest.  Clean facilities.

reviews.author: Ed R.
reviews.text: Favorite campground in the country!

reviews.author: Sara S.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground, very inviting rangers. Cannot wait to stay again!

reviews.author: Clifton G.
reviews.text: Snagged a site without prior reservation around 5:00PM mid-week.  Check in at ranger station for available sites.

reviews.author: Danielle M.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsite along the river

reviews.author: Marcia  J.
reviews.text: Absolutely beautiful place. Restrooms were clean, people were friendly, great hikes - it’s our favorite place.

reviews.author: Cecil H.
reviews.text: Very good sites.

reviews.author: Ken M.
reviews.text: Incredibly beautiful.  A lot of help at the ranger station.  I wish I could walk my dog in the park.  But the rangers had a ton of alternatives.

reviews.author: Dave  G.
reviews.text: Great campsites, well maintained facilities, lots of easy hiking from the campground.  Our site C11 was flat but had gravel where we pitched the tent so you might want extra padding under the tent floor for comfort.

reviews.author: Kelcie S.
reviews.text: Loved our quiet private sweet spot right on the river!

reviews.author: Catherine L.
reviews.text:
If you're young and strong, this is a great site as it's a walk-in site, up a big hill, then, down a long path.  I'm female and 60+. Thank God for the Ranger who helped me get all my gear up there with 2 dogs in tow!  
It was the last available site at the park and I had to take it because my dogs freak out from fireworks.  The site sits just above and to the left of its nearest site, making it a great site for close friends who want to camp close but in different sites. The site is small and adequate for 2 to 4 people in one larger tent.  (A family.)  I had great neighbors!
There are bathroom facilities at the top of the hill when you first come up, so it's not far from the site. Bring your own soap!  I don't think there was hot water and there are no showers but there are toilets, and it was clean. 
There was a clearing of tree branches above the site, so great spot for star gazing!!  
It had a nice firepit and table.  
The park itself is beautiful.

reviews.author: Joseph C.
reviews.text: First camping experience in Mount Rainier. Lovely campsite surrounded by primitive forest. Excellent trail to falls within campground.

reviews.author: Nathan A.
reviews.text:
Beautiful campground nestled in massive grove of trees, towering above all the sites. Plenty of coverage between sites to provide privacy, and tent sites were all level. Thankfully there were flush toilets and running water available in early October, with the nearest showers posted at the Ranger Station. 

Rangers who checked us in at the visitor center were helpful as always, providing plenty of recommendations on area hikes and letting us know the visibility of the mountain before setting out on the drive up to Paradise Visitor Center. Packwood nearby provided a grocery, gas, liquor stores and an adorable coffee & tea shop. Would love to visit again!

reviews.author: Julie S.
reviews.text: I have always wanted to camp here in the fall and it was beautiful! I've been camping here with my family for over 25 years but this time I camped solo.

reviews.author: Angela R.
reviews.text: beautiful campground on the white river

reviews.author: Michelle D.
reviews.text:
Ohanapecosh is wonderful this time of year. We made it to Paradise one day and Sunrise the next. It doesn’t get much better than that. Fires were allowed which was a bonus since we camped all summer long without. 
There are so many hiking trails in the area for everyone’s ability. Get the park maps and find a great one for the whole family to enjoy.

reviews.author: Erica H.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground with clean bathrooms

reviews.author: Angela A.
reviews.text: My favorite campground!

reviews.author: Bob P.
reviews.text: Quiet, clean campground with access to hiking trails right from the campground and/or a short drive away.

reviews.author: JINGYANG L.
reviews.text: Best camping site we’ve ever had in our 30 years camping. All covered under 50 ft+ cedar trees shade, fantastic!! A black bear showed up twice during our 5 day stay;-)

reviews.author: VICKI J.
reviews.text: Plenty of clean campsites easily accessed, quiet, clean bathrooms!

reviews.author: Warren K.
reviews.text: Beautiful surroundings. But no showers or hookups.

reviews.author: Phylis W.
reviews.text: EXCEPTIONAL EXPERIENCE! Check in was easy. Staff were personable, helpful and pleasant. Campground was absolutely beautiful! Very well maintained. Bathrooms kept clean. Highly, Highly recommend this campground!!!!

reviews.author: Matthew O.
reviews.text:
Nice campground although they were doing paving so we had to move sites.

Most driveways are small and not very level so it is only good for smaller travel trailers, camper vans, or tents.

Great hike to Silver Falls right from the campground.

reviews.author: Niall C.
reviews.text: Awesome. Hike to the falls and then on to The Grove of the Patriarchs.

reviews.author: Tina S.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground. Plenty of hiking opportunities. Excellent location

reviews.author: Mark C.
reviews.text: We loved this campground (more so than Cougar Rock). Unfortunately, we got there late in the season (September) and several loops were either closed for the season or for construction. Staff were wonderful (even the construction staff) and the setting was beautiful. Would recommend!!

reviews.author: Thomas L.
reviews.text: Very popular place (yet they have over 100 sites).  Did hike to nearby hot-springs, silver falls (about 1.5 miles away), and then "grove of the patriarchs" with some old and BIG trees (about another 1.5 miles). Lots of places inside Mt Rainier NP with this at the SE corner of it.

reviews.author: Allison  F.
reviews.text: This campsite located east of Mount Rainier is great! It is relatively close to some great Mount Rainier lookout spots such as Sunrise. All of the typical amenities we needed for camping was available at the campground and the ranger at the visitors center was very helpful in answering all of our questions.

reviews.author: Angela A.
reviews.text: I was surprised to see that FF is now managed by a ranger.  It seems like a lot of work for them, however it’s definitely more organized and I liked having a ranger presence this time of year.  The ranger working the check in desk was friendly, informative and helpful.  Overall a great experience once again at Ohanapecosh.  It’s my favorite place to camp!

reviews.author: Shari J.
reviews.text: We arrived without a reservation but had no problem finding a site.  The staff were very flexible and helpful.

reviews.author: Alice H.
reviews.text: Good camping, but sorry that we were forced into just loops A & B when we visited the weeknights after Labor Day.  It would be nice if they allowed people to spread out once the summer crowds and reserved sites were done.

reviews.author: Tom P.
reviews.text: Very nice site. Not noisy, which is a plus for us seniors. The ranger suggested we stay in a much smaller site, perhaps because we don't have an RV, but we found a nicer one and went with that.

reviews.author: Tom E.
reviews.text: The Silver Falls Loop Trail is addictive.

reviews.author: Paul S.
reviews.text: Great campground in a beautiful forest with lots of very large trees, near the river, and large campsites.  Most sites had good spacing and privacy.  Very quiet!

reviews.author: Greg F.
reviews.text: Good central location to visit both Paradise and Sunrise. Excellent hiking throughout the National Park!

reviews.author: Carol S.
reviews.text: This is just a wonderful park. Very quiet and peaceful. The most noise you will hear is the river flowing through the center of the park. Thank you to all the rangers who keep the grounds so pristine.

reviews.author: Rod S.
reviews.text: Beautiful weather and scenery.   No bugs!   Not overly crowded.

reviews.author: Jenn J.
reviews.text: Had a great time.

reviews.author: Lisa O.
reviews.text: We really enjoyed our lakeside spacious campground at Ohanapecosh. We had ample shade and a nice walking area throughout the campground. The ranger station nearby provided ample information and a nice walking path behind it to a hot water spring. The restrooms were clean and easy to access. Water was clean and potable at this and all of the national Park campgrounds we visited this trip.  We enjoyed going to nearby Paradise Lodge to hike Skyline Hike on Mount Rainier with great views of the mountains and lots of nature.

reviews.author: Jorge P.
reviews.text:
Great little campground with friendly rangers.

A4 was a fantastic spot, tucked away by a small stream. Spacious, pretty flat, and not too far from restrooms. Lucked out. 

Disappointed to see 4 campfires roaring around us despite the fire ban, but there was no one around to enforce.

reviews.author: Robert K.
reviews.text: Yearly visitor here, we enjoy the river and just hanging out at our campsite. We end up picking a nearby hike such as silver falls, grove of the patriarchs, or a little drive up to the naches peak loop or the sunrise area.

reviews.author: Jessie O.
reviews.text: Great campground! Really big but we didn’t feel too close to other sites. It’s a fairly easy hike to silver falls from the campground, and it’s well worth it! Gorgeous area.

reviews.author: Carol R.
reviews.text: The hike from the campground to Silver Falls was lovely. The campground itself is wooded and shady, although not much screening vegetation between sites. I would definitely stay here again.

reviews.author: Changhui X.
reviews.text: Only bathrooms need upgrade

reviews.author: idar r.
reviews.text: Good midpoint between Sunrise and Paradise to camp among the old forest trees. Restrooms clean and staff are helpful.

reviews.author: Andrew B.
reviews.text: The rangers and naturalists were extremely helpful.

reviews.author: Roberta d.
reviews.text: I have been many times and generally love it. This trip surprised me with how filthy my campsite was from prior campers leaving paper wrappers etc. It was disappointing. Maybe it was a fluke but it seemed to be cumulative since many papers were quite old.  Restrooms were clean.

reviews.author: Stephanie U.
reviews.text: This is my favorite campground in the park! Great vibes, great Rangers, lots to do within walking distance

reviews.author: Dan N.
reviews.text: It is just a beautiful location and has wonderful hiking trails near and around the campground. Some of the sites are small and awkward but in general a beautiful place!

reviews.author: Gary S.
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful campgrounds I have stayed at, great location in the park. Very clean, had good space between other campgrounds, the ranger was very nice and helpful as well.

reviews.author: Tiffany T.
reviews.text: campground is nice and clean and easy access to some hiking trails. It's also centrally located between Sunrise and Paradise. Very beautiful campground. Our site was not as private as I would like to have had it and as it was pictured on website, but other sites are more private. The river right in the campground is gorgeous. No hunting for firewood allowed and I didn't see any to buy at the campground either but that may be because fires were banned when we went. Might want to bring firewood just in case not available when allowed. Not much available within park for food, ice or other needs so make sure to bring all you need. Nice bear proof food storage lockers at every site.

reviews.author: Rob  M.
reviews.text: Our first time at Ohanapecosh and my family loved it! Clean, spacious campsite, plenty of walks/hikes that are family friendly, incredible trees, and a 15 minute car ride to so much more. We will be back.

reviews.author: Ly-Lan M.
reviews.text: Had a blast exploring Mt. Rainier from Ohanapecosh. Still a long drive to Paradise and Sunrise but at least we could beat the crowds. I did not realize just how remote the site was from a gas station/general store/internet connection. Only stayed for 3 days so ok but it might have been harder if we were off the grid for much longer. The Silver Falls and Grove of the Patriarch Trails were very easy to access. Kids enjoyed jumping into the creek to cool off after a long day of hiking.

reviews.author: Patrick H.
reviews.text: This place is amazing. Impossible to be disappointed

reviews.author: Megan S.
reviews.text:
The site was very spacious and flat. Loved that there was a lockable bear box available for each site. Bathrooms, water and trash were fairly close by. Flush toilets is always a plus! 
Only minor downsides would be that the sites on the inside of the loops are less private and when large groups stay up late and party the sound travels throughout the campground (bring earplugs just in case!)

reviews.author: Lee Z.
reviews.text: It’s a beautiful place and a great location, but it’s a little bit lacking in privacy, at least in the D loop where we were. Lots of very tall trees but little undergrowth. But we enjoyed it.

reviews.author: alena d.
reviews.text: This place is beautiful and clean. The hiking trails are awesome and there is a lot to choose from.

reviews.author: Pratik B.
reviews.text: Excellent campground right in the middle of the river. Just wish people follow the rules and don’t bring dogs on trails and camping area

reviews.author: deborah l.
reviews.text: Beautiful site. Great Location.

reviews.author: Jenise R.
reviews.text: Nice sites, great hikes right out of campground, good restrooms.

reviews.author: CRYSTAL S.
reviews.text: Good size campsites, fun day use area, easy access to trails, quiet.

reviews.author: Joseph F.
reviews.text: Clean, well laid out campsite in a gorgeous setting.  The rangers were very friendly and wonderful to our children.  There is a burn ban on effect, but they will let you bring in and use a propane fueled fire pit, which helps to preserve an important part of the camping experience for my family.

reviews.author: Chad U.
reviews.text: Thoroughly enjoyed my stay!  I had a reservation for one night and got a first come site for the next two days with no trouble.  A Loop was plenty quiet and calm, no loud parties.  The only things that went wrong were out of the campground's control: COVID shutting down events and smoke from being downwind of a big fire northeast of the mountain.  Flush toilets, potable water, all the goodies.  Would recommend staying here.

reviews.author: dawn s.
reviews.text: Easy check in.  Great location on the river.  Quiet campground.  Sites are well maintained.  Secure refuse containers.  Clean bathrooms located in each loop.  Campground hosts on site and rangers wete observed checking grounds daily.

reviews.author: Donald P.
reviews.text: x

reviews.author: Chris O.
reviews.text: Beautiful.

reviews.author: Karl S.
reviews.text: Beautiful, quiet and clean camping in a beautiful surrounding. Personally loved the water nearby and playing in the river. Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Taylor W.
reviews.text: Very beautiful and the campsite was well taken care of.

reviews.author: Melissa R.
reviews.text: Very fun campground. There is access to the river from the campground. The water was cold and clean! My family and I spent a whole day in the water.

reviews.author: Rebecca K.
reviews.text:
Beautiful trees but no privacy as there isn’t much of an understory (bushes, etc.) in most sites, so no visual barriers between sites. For us this meant a family of 10-12 people just ten feet away who frequently walked right through our campsite and the next one to get to the bathrooms and water. 

The river and trails are beautiful.

reviews.author: Christopher F.
reviews.text: The absolute best campground in the national park system. I hate to leave a good review because that means more people will visit... but everyone deserves to spend some time here. Perfect family camping

reviews.author: Alice J.
reviews.text: Beautiful spacious camp ground with a gorgeous river running thru it.   Great access for either the Sunrise side of the mountain or the Paradise side.

reviews.author: Carol M.
reviews.text: We had a great camping experience. A few observations: not all campsites had a bear box, not clear why that is the case. There was a fully burn ban on and we were disappointed that two families near us had wood fires anyway.

reviews.author: Janella R.
reviews.text: Our particular site was not very private (last available when I reserved) and the people next to us happened to be the noisiest ones in the whole loop. Aside from that, the campground was very clean and everything went smoothly. We really enjoyed the hikes in the area and our time by the river.

reviews.author: Angel O.
reviews.text: Camp is wonderful. Well kept/maintained/serviced. Fire ban in place was a bummer but needed and well-understood.  Loop A facilities are older and had no showers but a few dunks in the very cold river made up for it (well worth it!). Stay next to the river if you can!

reviews.author: Danielle W.
reviews.text:
The campground is absolutely gorgeous! My family loved the x2 hikes that started at the campground. I loved walking around the loops.  I do think it would be helpful if they had signage stating where the water/ river access points are located. I would also LOVE a shower location, if they had that I would stay there the maximum amount of time allowed! Lol. 
Thank you for having a beautiful and clean campground, we loved our stay!

reviews.author: Itzel F.
reviews.text:
This campground is beautiful, surrounded by beautiful trees, with the river in the back. 
The restroom where clean, no showers. Really nice place to explore Mt. Rainier.

reviews.author: John S.
reviews.text: Beautiful setting.  Easy hiking nearby.

reviews.author: Li H.
reviews.text: Great location for campsite, close to many trail heads for easy access to trails.  Clean bathrooms and sites. It’s nice they have generator times ending early so do not need to hear them all night.

reviews.author: Kristin P.
reviews.text: Great campground - sites were spacious and well maintained. No cell service, so enjoy the tranquility and listen to the creek if you're close enough. Great for a family trip.

reviews.author: CARLOS CESAR M.
reviews.text: Super nice campground. We really enjoy this place. Wonderful river, One of the best campgrounds I ever been. Super nice for families.

reviews.author: Bryelle M.
reviews.text: Super clean, fresh water, lots of fun activities, and helpful rangers.

reviews.author: Cecil H.
reviews.text: Just spent one night here at site overlooking the river. Large trees overhead but clear sight below. Family friendly access to river at the end of the loop.

reviews.author: Lue Ping Z.
reviews.text: We love the camp site: peaceful, close to nature, and well-maintained.  The only concern is that the site host was not clearly identified.  When we need to report a violation to the burn-ban, we could not get the help we need.  So it would be good to address.

reviews.author: Elena S.
reviews.text: Great campground, the only problem was that several ladies restrooms were out of soap and it was not refilled during our stay.

reviews.author: Priyanka M.
reviews.text: Very good experience.

reviews.author: Gabrielle C.
reviews.text: Beautiful and well kept!

reviews.author: Justin G.
reviews.text: Beautiful northwest campground!  1,000 year old trees and beautiful Silver Falls. Grove of the Patriarchs was incredible!  Helpful rangers and clean campsites!  Can’t wait to go back!

reviews.author: Nathan T.
reviews.text: I did a hike on the Silver Falls Trail. It was beautiful.

reviews.author: Barbara G.
reviews.text: We spent 3 days in Mount Rainier NP . What an amazing place .  We extended our stay for 2 additional nights at first come first serve campsite. Great place great location great service!

reviews.author: EMILY S.
reviews.text: This is an amazing campground with lots of allure. The hike to the waterfall and the river beach access were both highlights for our stay. The lush forest is an amazing setting to relax, unwind, and detach from the hustle and bustle. Rainier National Park offers lots to do and amazing views of a majestic mountain that is certainly worth the trip.

reviews.author: Krystal P.
reviews.text: Ohanapecosh is now one of my favorite campsites!!! I had a reservation for night 1, the site was very big and roomie with no neighbors as the next site was closed due to hazardous trees. I then got a FCFS site the next day (Wednesday AM); this was a fairly easy process that required being at the ranger office by around 730 or 800am. I believe they still had FCFS by around 1200p that day. The next site was smaller and closer to neighbors with little privacy. However, the campers were all very respectful of space and its one of the quietest campgrounds I've ever been too, despite how big it is! The creek and river run through the campground and at night you hear the river running which was soothing and glorious. All the facilities are very clean and well-maintained. Lots to explore with the river and Silver Falls Trail Loop right from the campground. Many loops and sites to fit every type of camper's needs. Will be going back yearly!

reviews.author: Steve W.
reviews.text: I want to thank the ranger staff for being so efficient in helping me with my issue. When I arrived someone had parked their car in my reserved spot and left the area. Instead of having to wait an indeterminate length of time for them to return, the rangers found me another site in which I could set up camp. We really appreciate their timely help!

reviews.author: Priyanka S.
reviews.text: Fantastic campground! Not very buggy during our trip either. There is some construction/road closure on the road leading to campground but luckily we didn’t get caught in it! About 45 minutes to Paradise.

reviews.author: Brian T.
reviews.text: Great campground and campsite, space 19 in loop A. Clear restrooms as close to the river. Nice hike up to the grove of the Patriarch’s right from the visitor center.

reviews.author: Susan L.
reviews.text: Stunning campground. Great hiking, quiet atmosphere, limited rv spaces--more geared for tent camping. Beautiful!

reviews.author: Robert M.
reviews.text: Beautiful old growth forest campsite. Not for extra long truck trailer combinations over 40'.

reviews.author: Susie Y.
reviews.text: Always clean! Great having a bear box at each site. Our site was next to the road/bridge and right above the river. The sound of the river was soothing and we didn’t hear much road noise or other campsite noise. Easy access to Paradise and Sunrise! Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Henrieta R.
reviews.text:
One of the most peaceful and well-designed national park campgrounds. Sounds of the mountain stream were an added bonus. Rangers were very helpful. We'd love to come back soon.
At first, we missed the turnout to the camp since all road signs were removed due to the road construction.

reviews.author: Rob L.
reviews.text: Very peaceful campground that’s walking distance to many beautiful trails and waterfalls.  If you have a tow vehicle, highly recommend taking the drive to Paradise Camp and its numerous trails up to the glacier.

reviews.author: Steven J.
reviews.text:
I can't say enough great things about Ohanapecosh Campground. I have been there several times recently and I'm always finding new adventures to take. There are a number of easy and more challenging trails right from the campground, plus the river to explore that runs right through the campground. It is also situated about 45 minutes from Paradise and about 60 minutes from Sunrise, which are both "must see" destinations for further exploring. The scenery is stunning, campsites and grounds are kept extremely clean and the wild flowers in summer are amazing!

I suggest you arrive at Paradise or Sunrise early (before 7AM) on summer weekends and before 8AM on summer week days to avoid lines getting into the parking lots.

reviews.author: CHRISTOPHER P.
reviews.text: What a great place, even in the dense standby campsite we got it was a quality experience. Luckily we got there on a heatwave and could survive hopping into the river

reviews.author: Huayun G.
reviews.text: Camp site E005 is great!

Looking for to spending more time here next time.

reviews.author: Caroline B.
reviews.text: This was our second trip to Ohanapecosh Campground this summer and we had an absolutely fabulous camping experience both times. Both of our stays were in A loop right on the river and it was a pleasure to see how much the river changed from swift and cold in mid July to a gentler flow in early September. The best sites in the campground are definitely on the river but the location can't be beat for exploring the whole park. Wonderful hikes right in the Ohanapecosh area and easy, highly scenic drives to both Sunrise and Paradise. Recommend!

reviews.author: Vamsi T.
reviews.text: Our stay at the campsite was wonderful. The site has all the essential amenities, the site was spacious, the washrooms were clean and there was adequate distance between the sites so that there is no disturbance and/or noise. There are ton of attractions and hiking spots in driving range, we woke up early and drove to sunrise point in the morning which was great.

reviews.author: Rebecca H.
reviews.text: The campground itself is great - I’ve stayed twice and it’s large and well maintained. Our site (B009) would not be a good fit for large tents. We had a couple small tents (2- and 3-person) and had trouble finding flat spots for them, although it did end up working out for us. Close to the bathrooms but we weren’t bothered by them at all. The site says it’s isolated, but we were right between two other sites - that said, there were enough trees between sites that we didn’t feel exposed. Love the campground, but would probably pick a different site next time if I came with a larger tent.

reviews.author: Paul D.
reviews.text: Quiet and peaceful family oriented with lots of easy bicycling around the loops. Plenty of hiking trails nearby from super easy to difficult. Nice, well kept bathrooms with a dish sink and water fountains in each loop. Wonderful helpful rangers but sadly no more evening presentations due to COVID. We stayed almost a week with different people coming and going in the sites around us and we made some great friends!

reviews.text: Very close to our neighbors with little privacy. That being said it’s a beautiful CG with river access and excellent swimming holes. Great family friendly hikes nearby - wish we could of stayed longer.  Clean bathrooms, fresh water and friendly rangers. What more do you need.

reviews.text: Covid19 put a kink in our plans, but it worked out with some diligent searching, walking, asking, and looking for a replacement site for our cancelled reserved site. It might have been wise to cancel the first few weeks of reservations to clear the hazard trees, then enable the entire campground to be open for the rest of the season.  Seems more fiscally sound and safer in the long run.

I really enjoyed staying here. With half the campsites closed for problem trees privacy was pretty good. Except we were on a direct path to the the bathroom and river so had people walking by pretty regularly. Next time we’ll try for a site near the river. 
As for getting into the park proper, I think this is the way to go. We never saw a line and could have gone all the to Paradise if we chose. Instead we just enjoyed the trails close by.

reviews.author: Evan B.
reviews.text:
This campsite is at the end of a row and backs directly onto the serene Ohanapecosh River with massive trees providing cover from the sun. It is drive-up, with packed earth, a firepit with grilling grate, a log for sitting, a picnic table, and bearproof storage locker.

Because this particular site has a neighboring campsite on one side only, and that site was unoccupied, it often felt as though we had the campsite to ourselves. At the nearby day use area there is a wading area in the river where the current slows (the water is freezing!), the bathrooms were clean, and there is potable water near the bathrooms. The firewood person comes by between 5-7pm, bundles are small, include kindling, and are $7.

The rangers are informative and friendly and advised us that we could keep our food in our car (whereas in Yosemite, for example, this is unadvisable). The amphitheater is currently closed due to COVID.

Overall, this is a perfect point from which to explore Mt. Rainier National Park, right at the foot of the road to Paradise. We will definitely be back.

reviews.text: We stayed in loop A, site 29. The overall campground was fantastic as far as cleanliness, amenities and the beauty of the nature but the campsites (at least in loop A) were WAY too close together. When we arrived, we actually thought that our neighbor had put up their tent on our site because they're that close. We may have gotten an open spot because a family out of a group dropped out, because the whole time we stayed the people to our right and left constantly walked through our site to get to their friends. It's a shame, because so many other sites look private/more secluded and spacious but we felt totally bottled in and not comfortable to spend a lot of time at our campsite. No other complaints about the campground or park, but really investigate where your spot is before booking .. or get ready to be constantly exposed to your neighbors.

reviews.text: Ohanapecosh is one of our family’s favorite campgrounds. It’s a lovely wooded setting with a stream to swim in. Rushing blue waters and a waterfall are only a short walk away. There’s even a small volcanic hot spring. Convenient to the major attractions of Mt Rainier NP.

reviews.author: Sunday W.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground, but the facility was packed and section where we camped was occupied by several families who were using generators to watch outdoor movies projected onto sheets at night, and used a commercial PA system for the sound. A family with a toddler next to us left in the dark to go drive to a hotel for the night after reporting the event to the camp host, who did not come to intervene. The next day we explained the situation to the rangers as well as the camp host, who told us that it wasn't worth the conflict to ask the families to stop. The families played music over their PA system all day, and then projected movies again at night. They also dragged full logs from the surrounding forest to burn in a shared bonfire, which is a federal misdemeanor. Again we told the rangers who did not intervene. I can't imagine returning to this campsite knowing there's no support from rangers or camp hosts.
