reviews.text: This was our favorite camping spot with kids at Mount Rainier we loved the hike and waterfalls and the visitor nature center was perfect for a family with kids. Thanks for a beautiful memory

reviews.author: Rodney M.
reviews.text: Weather was cooperative and the site was well set up for camping. Our site had good access to the bathroom and was reasonably isolated from other sites. Campground is close to " Grove of the Patriarchs " and we love the river running through it.

reviews.author: Joel A.
reviews.text: We got a great site next to the river.  Swam in the icy water with the grandkids.   Great fun.   Nice evening program for kids.

reviews.author: KARLA G.
reviews.text: My family and I have been going to Ohanapecosh for over 40 years and we love it every time. All of the trails are great, love Silverfalls. The drive up to Paradise is amazing Everytime, so much to see and stops to make on the drive up. Mount Rainier is our mountain.

reviews.author: Chansey C.
reviews.text: This is a fantastic campground! Plenty of space in our site, well maintained overall, and washrooms were easy to find. Will definitely be back for another stay.

reviews.author: GEORGIA B.
reviews.text: I have been coming here for over 30 years. To me it is the most beautiful camping spot ever! We've hiked to Silver Falls many times and it is always breathtaking. I enjoy most the peace that comes with sitting around the campfire in the mornings with coffee and evenings with the fire, a good book and a glass of wine!

reviews.author: Kristin K.
reviews.text: Great campground! So many fun activities for kids as well as the hiking and swimming

reviews.author: John B.
reviews.text: Lovely campground in a beautiful setting. Facilities are well maintained.  But I (and others in our section) were disturbed by one camper running a very loud generator for a couple hours! Certainly takes away from the outdoor experience.  Apparently,  this is allowed by the campground rules during certain hours. But I wonder if the rules could include an overall length of time allowed.

reviews.author: Benton M.
reviews.text:
Staying at Ohanapecosh is always a lovely experience -- which we've done at least twice a year for many years. Just the right balance of beautiful trees, natural, clean and functional camp sites, the necessary amenities, hiking to beautiful Silver Falls and Grove of the Patriarchs and of course the always wonderful Ohanapecosh river. 

We have traveled a lot, but getting back to Ohanapecosh is what we greatly look forward to doing every year. Fully enjoyable and relaxed every time.

reviews.author: Maddie R.
reviews.text: This was a great anchor point for exploring the park! It offered really great river access and was in close proximity to outside towns for grocery/gas access. It gets a bit loud, which did not bother us, but is good to note. Would highly recommend for families/big groups!

reviews.author: David P.
reviews.text: The park was easy to navigate. The campsites were large and fairly private. The campground was clean as were the restrooms. Staff was friendly and the park visit was excellent!

reviews.author: Allison D.
reviews.text: We camped for 2 nights in August in the C loop, and loved it. Great location in the park, not too far from anything. Highly recommend the Silver Falls hike located off the B loop. Easy hike with a stunning payoff.

reviews.author: David L.
reviews.text: Great shade spots.  Enjoy  visitor center and trails

reviews.author: David H.
reviews.text: Beautiful park, campground was very well located. Loved the nature trail behind thevisitors center. The people working at the visitors center were very polite and helpfull.

reviews.author: Melissa M.
reviews.text:
Everything was great- as usual. We REALLLLLLLLLY miss the ability to dump before driving our 4.5 hrs home. 
Staff were friendly, trails were maintained. The only thing we noticed is it is becoming harder to pull into our usual spot with our truck and trailer bc of tree and bush growth. 
It’s still one of our favorite summer vacations! 
Thanks for all you do!

reviews.author: Tamara C.
reviews.text: Ohanapecosh is stunning.

reviews.author: Robin F.
reviews.text: Walking to Silver Falls is wonderful . . . on the east side trail as it crosses many streams.  The Visitor Center is a good place for information.

reviews.author: Linda S.
reviews.text: Really nice camprgound. More remote tham others in park.

reviews.author: Michael B.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground with somewhat limited facilities for a developed campground (no showers for example).  We were there in July and it was crowded, but still had some private space.   Plenty of good hiking nearby.

reviews.author: Lara L.
reviews.text: Relaxing and quiet. It was wonderful.

reviews.author: Richard R.
reviews.text: Ohanapecosh has been a family destination for decades. Well-kept campground, friendly rangers. Stunning scenery in the Park.

reviews.author: Jessica P.
reviews.text: Gorgeous area and fun to play in the river in between hikes.

reviews.author: Molly H.
reviews.text: beautiful & well-maintained - the only issue was it was hard to track down the ranger selling firewood and waiting for when he started selling it- would have been so much easier if he just stayed at the ranger station and let us come to him....

reviews.author: Holly R.
reviews.text: Beautiful camping! Come here every single year. Love the hiking trail nearby. Quick hike with littles. Best views.

reviews.author: Julie S.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground perfectly located in Mt. Rainier National Park along a river. Quiet campground and it was super easy to book a campground and find our site. Fire pits are really nice here and make cooking easy!

reviews.author: Ann B.
reviews.text: The river in the campground is beautiful and when we were there, our kids chose to go wading. Bring a swimsuit and towel just in case!

reviews.author: Debbie B.
reviews.text: We camp at Ohanapecosh every year because of its rustic nature, dark skies and the fact that we can hear the sound of wind in the trees.  The toilet and water facilities are more than adequate and the campsites well- spaced.

reviews.author: Wayne M.
reviews.text: Camping in Ohanapecosh causes one to reflect on the old-school family camping trips, with a tent nestled in between old-growth forest giants, clear babbling brooks lulling one to sleep, and an experience taken in at a slower, less hectic pace than our normal lives.  This is the ONLY campground to which we return year after year, and will continue to do so...come join us by our campfire and sit a spell:-)

reviews.author: Leah B.
reviews.text: Beautiful, just a few yards from a water view

reviews.author: Eric N.
reviews.text: Our favorite campground for visiting Rainier National Park!

reviews.author: Robert K.
reviews.text: Of all the campsites I visited on a three-month road trip last summer, the Ohanapecosh Campground stood above all the rest. My buddy and I had a terrific site next to the river in old-growth forest. Good bathroom facilities. Excellent location for exploration around Mt. Rainier. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Kanon M.
reviews.text: This campground’s made our family’s annual camping rotation.   It is, hands down, one of most beautiful campgrounds we’ve ever visited.  The rest of Mt. Rainier National Park is just icing on the cake.

reviews.author: Georgia J.
reviews.text: Loved our campsite. The park was nice and very clean. Staff were professional. My daughter went to the kids program every day, they were excellent. The one thing that I would have loved would be a hot shower, but I understand why they don't have any. Hoping to go back again next summer. ❤❤

reviews.author: Mary D.
reviews.text: Great location for launching Mt. Rainier activities.

reviews.author: John B.
reviews.text: This is our favorite campground in Washington. Sites are large and private. Nice family friendly hike to Silver Falls and the Grove of the Patriarchs.  The river has several good swimming holes

reviews.author: Douglas K.
reviews.text: I love Ohanapecosh.  The rangers and staff are always pleasant and very helpful.  The campsites are spacious.  And, it's just plain beautiful.

reviews.author: Steven W.
reviews.text: My favorite campground in Washington!

reviews.author: Renee D.
reviews.text: This is a beautiful campground with a good number of larger sites. Great ranger talks and the campground hosts keep the place neat and tidy.

reviews.author: Steven S.
reviews.text: Campsite was inspiring with tall trees, sturdy table, spacious area and sound of river.  The campground was quiet and beautiful.

reviews.author: Tony D.
reviews.text: Some of my oldest and fondest memories are camping with my Family at Ohanapecosh!! I have been coming here for over 45 years. The thing that I like and appreciate the most is that except for a few minor exceptions (Fewer ranger programs at the Amphitheater and more people) it is the same campground it was 45 years ago when my family discovered it. Now I bring my boys and they absolutely LOVE IT! In fact my 10yo. wanted his 10th birthday party at Ohanapecosh this year. So we brought my family and 10 of his friends and they had a blast riding, hiking, roasting marsh mellows etc.......  so much so he has said he wants this years party at Ohanapecosh again this year. I hope it NEVER changes! All I can say is This is a Treasured Resource that ALL Americans should experience at least once even for a day trip to the great Visitor Center.

reviews.author: Peggy M.
reviews.text: Lovely campground with several hikes right from you sites.  The Grove of the Patriarchs is a stand of old growth trees, close to the campground is a must see wonder!

reviews.author: Hugh S.
reviews.text: Beautiful setting, sounds of the river below, friendly neighbors, reasonably priced firewood, clean restrooms. Great loop hike up to Silver Falls.
